| A ball or wheel rolls forever | [Rolling without damping](#spheres-roll-forever) |
| State reads return zeros or stale values; `views.curr.byteLength` is 0 | [Detached views](#state-views-read-zeros-after-a-spawn) |
| `raycast` returns false on a world you just built | [Raycast before the first step](#raycasts-miss-on-a-new-world) |
| You need collision callbacks | [No contact events](#there-are-no-contact-events) |
| A bad scene reports one error at a time | [One scene error](#only-the-first-scene-error-is-reported) |
| The sidecar `stateHash` is the same in every capture | [stateHash of the idle world](#the-shot-statehash-never-changes) |
| `!important` vanished from a CSS file after a lint fix | [biome --unsafe](#biome---unsafe-removed-important) |
| A worker-based sim makes fixed-mode captures flaky or time out | [Worker in fixed mode](#fixed-mode-captures-with-a-worker-sim) |
| fps looks fine (or terrible) but was measured headless, on SwiftShader or only on WebGL | [Untrustworthy fps](#fps-from-a-headless-or-webgl-run-is-misleading) |
| `SyntaxError [ERR_UNSUPPORTED_TYPESCRIPT_SYNTAX]: TypeScript parameter property is not supported in strip-only mode` | [Parameter properties in Node](#parameter-properties-fail-in-a-node-script) |
| A night or indoor scene is too bright; no point lights in the scene JSON | [Night scenes](#a-night-scene-is-too-bright) |
| Draw calls climb fast with each skinned character | [Shadow cascades multiply draws](#draw-calls-climb-with-each-character) |
| Flat decals on a splat floor get ink outlines in the toon style | [Decal outlines](#decals-on-a-splat-floor-get-ink-outlines) |
| A bench copied from another game reports numbers for the wrong scene, or never connects | [Copied fps bench](#a-copied-fps-bench-measures-the-wrong-thing) |

## BackendUnavailable: webgpu

**Symptom:** `BackendUnavailable: webgpu (WebGPURenderer fell back to WebGL)` on the page, in `__pebble3d.error`, or as a `pnpm shot` failure.

**Cause:** the browser exposed no usable WebGPU adapter, so three's `WebGPURenderer` fell back to WebGL, and `createRenderer` (`packages/renderer/src/create.ts`) throws when `webgpu` was requested. On Linux, Chromium often ships with WebGPU off; open `chrome://gpu` and look at the WebGPU line to check.

**Fix:**
- Start Chromium with `chromium --enable-unsafe-webgpu --enable-features=Vulkan --use-angle=vulkan`. `pnpm shot` already passes these (plus `--ignore-gpu-blocklist`).
- Or use the WebGL fallback: `?backend=webgl` in the URL, `--backend webgl` for `pnpm shot`.
- Or opt in to the automatic fallback: `createGame({ ..., webglFallback: true })` (or `createRenderer`'s `webglFallback`), a build with `VITE_PEBBLE3D_WEBGL_FALLBACK=1`, or `?webglFallback=1` in the URL. The renderer then keeps WebGL on the same canvas and shows a small dismissible notice. It is off by default so a missing WebGPU fails loudly. The public demo builds turn it on.
- The playground falls back by itself only when no `backend` param is given (`apps/playground/src/main.ts`, `isBackendUnavailable`). Your own app must do the same if it wants a fallback, and must retry on a fresh canvas, because a canvas keeps its first context type:

```ts
const fresh = canvas.cloneNode() as HTMLCanvasElement;
canvas.replaceWith(fresh);
game = await createGame({ ...opts, canvas: fresh, backend: "webgl" });
```

## WebGL outdoor scene is black or white

**Symptom:** on the WebGL fallback (`?backend=webgl`, Firefox/Safari), an `outdoor` scene with an HDRI renders almost entirely black with fog on, or blown-out white with fog off. The sky itself may still be visible with bloom off. WebGPU, and the `studio` preset, look fine.

**Cause:** `HDRLoader` decodes to half floats, so the sun of a bright HDRI (Poly Haven's `qwantani_noon_puresky_2k.hdr`) is stored as 65504, the half-float maximum. In three 0.187 both backends run the same `PMREMGenerator` with half-float targets, but empirically only the WebGL backend's PMREM overflows to +Inf on these fp16-max peaks (the exact step is unconfirmed). Every IBL-lit fragment then shades to +Inf (white after tone mapping), the range fog's `mix` turns that into NaN (black), and bloom spreads either over the frame. Measured on WebGL with a plain clamp: 32768 renders correctly, 60000 does not.

**Fix:** handled in `loadEnvironment` (`packages/renderer/src/defaults/lighting.ts`): on WebGL only, `spreadEquirectPeaks` caps HDRI texels at `WEBGL_HDR_MAX_RADIANCE` (16384, validated on WebGL with spreading) by scattering the excess into neighbouring texels, which conserves the sun's energy, so diffuse IBL matches WebGPU. The same capped HDRI is the WebGL background, so there the sun disc in the sky and in reflections is slightly wider and its peak lower (it still tone-maps to white). Non-finite texels are clamped, not spread. WebGPU loads the HDRI unchanged. If you load your own HDRI into a PMREM on WebGL outside `loadEnvironment`, run it through `spreadEquirectPeaks` first.

## Stale wasm: setVelocity is not a function

**Symptom:** `TypeError: world.setVelocity is not a function` (or `applyImpulse`, `linearVelocity`, `applyTorqueImpulse`, `setKinematicPose`), a scene feature that silently does nothing after a merge, or the sdk test `expect(h.world.scratchLen()).toBe(SCRATCH_LEN)` failing.

**Cause:** `packages/sdk/wasm/` is gitignored. A pull, merge or branch switch updates the Rust source and the TypeScript that calls it, but not the compiled wasm, so the JS calls methods the old binary lacks. In a fresh clone or worktree the folder is missing entirely and imports of `packages/sdk/wasm/det/engine_core_det.js` fail.

**Fix:** `pnpm build:wasm` (Rust, the `wasm32-unknown-unknown` target and `wasm-bindgen-cli` 0.2.130; `scripts/build-wasm.sh` checks the version). Run it after every Rust change or merge, then restart the dev server.

## Shot --out rejected

**Symptom:** `shot: FAIL --out must be inside artifacts/`.

**Cause:** `scripts/shot/shot.mjs` resolves `--out` against the repo root and refuses any directory outside `artifacts/` (gitignored), so shots never land in source folders.

**Fix:** `--out artifacts/<something>`, for example `pnpm shot --app rockfall --param demo=1 --out artifacts/rockfall-check`. Omit `--out` for the default `artifacts/shots/`.

## Shot refuses a SwiftShader adapter

**Symptom:** `shot: headless got a software adapter; retrying headed`, then `shot: FAIL software/fallback adapter (SwiftShader) refused: {...}`.

**Cause:** Chromium ran on its CPU rasteriser (SwiftShader) or a fallback adapter instead of the GPU. Timings and some rendering paths are meaningless there, so the shot refuses it. Headless Chromium reaches the real GPU only with `--use-angle=vulkan`; with a display available the shot retries headed once.

**Fix:**
- Run on a machine with a GPU and working Vulkan drivers, from a session with `DISPLAY` or `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` set (or pass `--headed`).
- An app with its own boot must report real adapter strings on `__pebble3d.adapterInfo`, or the check cannot work. Copy `adapterInfoOf` from `packages/sdk/src/game.ts`, as `apps/rockfall/src/main.ts` does; it reads the unmasked WebGL renderer string so `--backend webgl` on SwiftShader is still caught.

## Determinism hash mismatch

**Symptom:** `determinism mismatch: expected 2d76d9927e780425, got <other>` from `packages/sdk/test/determinism.mjs`, a shot sidecar `stateHash` that differs from the fixture at tick 1000, `pnpm --filter chain-reaction verify` failing a level, or a game's Node determinism test failing.

**Cause (check in this order):**
1. Stale wasm (see above): the binary is older or newer than the source.
2. An engine change that is not opt-in: it altered a default, the spawn order, or solver settings.
3. The sim reads `Math.random`, `Date`, wall-clock `dt` or DOM state.
4. The run used the `fast` build. It is deterministic only for the same binary on the same machine; the fixture is for `deterministic`.
5. Realtime mode ran 2+ ticks in one frame while game logic ran once per frame (input applied at a different tick). Fixed mode runs exactly one tick per frame.

**Fix:** `pnpm build:wasm`, then rerun the script. If it still differs, make the change opt-in so the defaults reproduce the old state. Move randomness to a seeded generator (`apps/rockfall/src/game/rng.ts`). Never run `determinism.mjs --write` to accept a new hash unless the change is meant to alter default behaviour and that has been agreed.

## Shot fails on a 404

**Symptom:** `shot: FAIL console error not allowlisted: Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404 (Not Found)`.

**Cause:** something requested a missing file. Two common ones:
- No `<link rel="icon">` in `index.html`, so the browser asks for `/favicon.ico`.
- A missing asset: `pnpm fetch-assets` was not run, or the app does not serve the playground's `public/`. Apps use `appType: "mpa"` in `vite.config.ts` so missing assets are real 404s, not a silent `index.html`.

**Fix:** add `<link rel="icon" type="image/svg+xml" href="/favicon.svg" />`; run `pnpm fetch-assets`; copy `vite.config.ts` from an existing app (`publicDir: "../playground/public"`). Rerun with `--headed` to see which URL failed in the network tab.

## Shot times out waiting for `__pebble3d.done`

**Symptom:** the shot waits for the full `--timeout` (default 60 s) and fails on `__pebble3d.done` (or `__pebble3d.ready`).

**Cause:**
- The app ignores `?mode=fixed&ticks=<n>`, so nothing sets `done`. `createGame` sets it only when it was given `mode: "fixed"` and `stopAtTick`.
- A custom boot (no `createGame`) never sets `window.__pebble3d.done`.
- `main()` threw before the first frame.

**Fix:** pass `mode` and `stopAtTick` from the URL to `createGame` ([getting-started.md](getting-started.md#srcmaints-boot-input-probes)). A custom boot sets `hook.done = true` once `tick >= stopAtTick` in fixed mode (`apps/rockfall/src/main.ts`). Catch boot errors into `window.__pebble3d.error` and `console.error` so the failure is visible.

## TS2352 when passing an imported scene JSON

**Symptom:** `error TS2352: Conversion of type '{ version: number; ... }' to type '...' may be a mistake ... Type 'number[]' is not comparable to type '[number, number, number]'.`

**Cause:** a JSON import widens `[0, 3, 8]` to `number[]`, which does not match the schema's tuple types.

**Fix:** cast through `unknown`; `createGame` validates the scene with zod at runtime anyway:

```ts
import sceneJson from "../scenes/court.json";
const scene = sceneJson as unknown as SceneInput;
```

## fps numbers are low or noisy

**Symptom:** a bench reports 20-50 fps, or results swing between runs, for a scene that should hold 60.

**Cause:** another process is using the GPU. Other GPU-heavy apps (browsers, video, builds, compositors) can drag fps well below what the scene really holds, so measure on an idle GPU.

**Fix:** check `/sys/class/drm/*/gpu_busy_percent` (Linux, AMD) before measuring, close other GPU users, and compare builds back to back in the same window. Use `BENCH_VSYNC=1` for the capped number players see ([verification.md](verification.md#benches-and-capture-scripts)).

## Heavy physics makes the game crawl

**Symptom:** with 1,000+ awake bodies each frame gets later and later, or the frame rate collapses.

**Cause:** in realtime mode `FixedStepLoop` catches up with up to 5 ticks per frame by default. When one tick costs more than a frame, each frame runs more ticks, which makes the next frame later still.

**Fix:**
- Cap catch-up: `new FixedStepLoop({ mode, maxTicksPerFrame: 2 })` (`apps/rockfall/src/main.ts`). The game slows down instead of spiralling.
- Use the `fast` build when you only need same-machine determinism: `"sim": { "build": "fast" }` halved Breakpoint's tick cost (about 26 ms to 13 ms at 1,300 awake bodies; `apps/breakpoint/scenes/site.json`).
- Move the sim to a Web Worker (`apps/breakpoint/src/game/sim.worker.ts`). Bound its message queue and pause on `visibilitychange`, or a hidden tab queues ticks without limit.

## fetch-assets hash mismatch or failed avatar

**Symptom:** `pnpm fetch-assets` prints `<url>: sha256 mismatch (expected ..., got ...)`, or reports the human avatar `rocketbox-male-adult-16.glb` as failed.

**Cause:** the derived splat hash was verified on one machine only. The avatar build needs the pinned KTX-Software binary, which is linux-x64 only.

**Fix:** for the avatar on other platforms, use `/?scene=showcase-robot`. For a hash mismatch, check the source download first; `node scripts/fetch-assets.mjs --update-hashes` rewrites hashes in the manifest, so use it only for assets you are adding.

## `pnpm docs` does nothing useful

**Symptom:** `pnpm docs` does not regenerate `docs/`.

**Cause:** `docs` is a pnpm builtin command, which shadows a script of that name.

**Fix:** `pnpm docs:gen`. `pnpm docs:gen --check` exits 1 when generated files are stale.

## scene.schema.json is stale

**Symptom:** the sdk test `scene-schema-json.test.ts` fails, the docs drift test reports `generated docs are current` failing, or two branches conflict in `packages/sdk/scene.schema.json`.

**Cause:** `packages/sdk/scene.schema.json` and `docs/scene-reference.md` are generated from `packages/sdk/src/schema.ts`.

**Fix:** never hand-merge them. Resolve `schema.ts`, then `pnpm --filter @pebble3d/sdk schema && pnpm docs:gen`.

## Two identical shots differ slightly

**Symptom:** two captures of the same tick are not byte-identical.

**Cause:** GPU rasterisation noise. Two runs of identical code measured 36 px over a 2% fuzz at about 53 dB PSNR on the showcase scene; screenshots repeat to RMSE < 0.002, not byte for byte.

**Fix:** compare `stateHash` and `tick` in the sidecars for logic, and a fuzzy image diff against a measured noise floor for rendering.

## createGame has no per-tick hook

**Symptom:** you need code to run exactly once per sim tick, or to see bodies that spawners created at runtime, and `createGame` offers only `onFrame`.

**Cause:** `createGame` steps the world itself and consumes `drainSpawned()` for the scene's spawners. There is no `onTick` or `onSpawned` callback yet.

**Fix:** for light rules, advance your own sim inside `onFrame` until it reaches `world.tick()` ([getting-started.md](getting-started.md#3-a-minimal-game-app)). For full control, boot like `apps/rockfall/src/main.ts`: `createRenderer` + `loadSim` + `FixedStepLoop`, your own `sim.step(input)` per tick, and your own `window.__pebble3d` hook. Or keep `createGame` for rendering and run your sim in separate worlds from the same wasm module (`engineFrom` in `apps/chain-reaction/src/puzzle/sim.ts`).

## A new app's tests never run

**Symptom:** `npx vitest run --project my-app` fails with `No projects were found ... The filter matched no projects: my-app`; `npx vitest run apps/my-app/test` prints `No test files found, exiting with code 0`; `pnpm test` passes without running your tests.

**Cause:** the root `vitest.config.ts` lists every project explicitly in `test.projects`; a folder under `apps/` is not picked up by itself.

**Fix:** add `apps/my-app/vitest.config.ts` (`defineProject({ test: { name: "my-app", include: ["test/**/*.test.ts"], testTimeout: 60_000 } })`, as `apps/rockfall/vitest.config.ts`) and add `"apps/my-app"` to `projects` in the root `vitest.config.ts`. Details: [getting-started.md](getting-started.md#tests-in-node).

## Headless hash differs from the browser

**Symptom:** a Node test reproduces a run, but `world.stateHash()` after n ticks is not the `stateHash` in the `pnpm shot --ticks n` sidecar.

**Cause:** usually the order of rules and physics. `createGame` runs `world.step` and then `onFrame`, so rules run after physics each tick; a Node loop that runs `sim.step(input)` before `world.step(1)` shifts tick-keyed rules by one tick. Other causes: a different seed or gravity in `loadSim` (pass `scene.sim.seed` / `scene.sim.gravity`), spawning entries in a different order than `expandScene(scene).sim`, the `fast` build, or JS math that differs between engines.

**Fix:** mirror the browser loop exactly: `world.step(1); views.refresh(); bot.next(sim, input); sim.step(input);` per tick for a `createGame` app, or call the sim's own `step()` if the sim owns its world. See [getting-started.md](getting-started.md#tick-order).

## A second game on the same page

**Symptom:** you call `createGame` again on the same page (level switch, site change) and the old game is still wired up.

**Cause:** `Game.dispose` does not exist yet. `game.stop()` only cancels the frame loop; the renderer, the wasm `World`, the window key listeners, the `ResizeObserver` and `window.__pebble3d` stay.

**Fix:** one game per page. Switch levels inside one game (new `World`s, as Chain Reaction does per run) or reload the page with new URL params (Field Notes reloads to change site).

## Assets 404 under a sub-path

**Symptom:** served from `/games/x/` instead of `/`, the console shows 404s for `/assets/...`, `/basis/basis_transcoder.js` or a `.wasm`.

**Cause:** a URL that bypasses the asset base. The renderer prefixes root-absolute URLs in the scene, in `renderer.loadGltf` and in the transcoder path with the asset base (`createGame`/`createRenderer` `assetBase`, else `VITE_PEBBLE3D_ASSET_BASE`, else Vite's `--base`). Your own `fetch`, `attachSound` and three.js loaders are not prefixed; neither are relative paths.

**Fix:** build with `vite build --base /games/x/`, keep asset paths root-absolute, pass hand-loaded URLs through `renderer.assetUrl(url)`, and copy `vite.config.ts` from `apps/rockfall` (it emits `basis/`). Full layout: [cookbook/sub-path-hosting.md](cookbook/sub-path-hosting.md).

## The orbit camera fights your camera

**Symptom:** you set `renderer.three.camera` every frame, yet a mouse drag or the wheel still nudges it, or touch scrolling is dead on the canvas.

**Cause:** the scene's `camera.controller` defaults to `"orbit"`, which attaches three's `OrbitControls` to the canvas. There is no `"none"` value. Setting `renderer.controller = null` stops its per-frame update but leaves its listeners, which update the camera themselves.

**Fix:** `renderer.controller?.dispose(); renderer.controller = null;` after boot, or use `"controller": "thirdPerson"` in a scene without a `character` (no controller is created). See [cookbook/custom-camera.md](cookbook/custom-camera.md).

## Your setCharacterInput is overwritten

**Symptom:** your rules call `world.setCharacterInput` for the player character inside the per-tick loop; at 60 Hz it works, on a 120 Hz or 144 Hz display the demo bot stops steering or the player still walks with the keyboard when your rules say stand still.

**Cause:** `createGame` sends `game.player.input` (the keyboard) with `setCharacterInput` every frame, including frames that run 0 ticks. On a fast display most frames run no tick, so the rig's value replaces yours before the next `world.step`.

**Fix:** re-send your intent at the end of every `onFrame`, after the tick loop (`apps/lanternfall/src/main.ts`, lines 82-91, and `assertInput` in `apps/lanternfall/src/game/sim.ts`, lines 403-420), or drive the player only by writing `game.player.input`.

## Other characters do not animate

**Symptom:** the first character animates; the others move but stay in their bind pose and never turn.

**Cause:** `createGame` builds a `CharacterView` (animation mixer and facing) only for `game.player`, the first entity with a `character`.

**Fix:** for each other character call `game.renderer.attachCharacter(simId, clipMap)` once, then per frame `world.characterState(simId)` and `view.update(frame, dt)` (`apps/lanternfall/src/view/present.ts`, lines 155-160 and 248-260). To make a different character the player, put it first in `entities`.

## A static mesh does not move

**Symptom:** `world.teleport` on a `"static"` body moves its collider (things bump into it at the new spot) but its mesh stays where it started.

**Cause:** the renderer places a static body's mesh once, on the first `renderer.sync` after it was added, and never reads its slot again.

**Fix:** make anything that moves `"kinematic"` and move it with `setKinematicPose` or `teleport`; its visual then follows every frame. Code that inspects or merges static meshes must run after the first frame.

## Spheres roll forever

**Symptom:** a ball on flat ground never slows down.

**Cause:** Rapier has no rolling resistance, and `angularDamping` and `linearDamping` default to 0.

**Fix:** set `"angularDamping"` on rolling bodies (0.25 in Pebble Garden's pebble, `apps/pebble-garden/src/garden/pieces.ts`, lines 156-163). Details: [cookbook/bodies-impulses-velocity.md](cookbook/bodies-impulses-velocity.md).

## State views read zeros after a spawn

**Symptom:** after spawning (or when running several worlds), `views.curr` / `views.scratch` read 0 or old values, positions jump to the origin, or a raycast result reads 0.

**Cause:** a spawn grew the wasm memory, which detaches every typed array over the old buffer. All worlds from one wasm module share that memory, so a spawn in any world detaches the views of all of them. `createGame` refreshes `game.views` once per frame; a world you create gets no such refresh.

**Fix:** call `views.refresh()` after spawning or stepping, and before reading scratch results, and read `views.curr` / `views.scratch` through the views object instead of keeping the arrays (`apps/swarm-siege/src/game/sim.ts`, lines 380-385). See [cookbook/owning-the-world.md](cookbook/owning-the-world.md).

## Raycasts miss on a new world

**Symptom:** `world.raycast` returns false on a world you just created and spawned, even straight down onto the floor.

**Cause:** queries use the broad phase as of the last `step`; a world that has never stepped has none.

**Fix:** `world.step(1)` once after spawning, before the first query, or defer the query work to the first tick (`apps/lanternfall/src/game/sim.ts`, lines 325-329).

## There are no contact events

**Symptom:** you look for an `onCollision` callback or a contact list and find none.

**Cause:** the engine does not expose Rapier's contact or intersection events.

**Fix:** detect contacts in your rules after each step from state you already read: centre distance and closing speed (`apps/ringout/src/game/sim.ts`, lines 341-404), or a velocity change the forces you applied do not explain (`apps/drift-drone/src/game/sim.ts`, lines 407-423 and 441-451). Trigger zones that only test a position need no body at all. Patterns: [cookbook/bodies-impulses-velocity.md](cookbook/bodies-impulses-velocity.md).

## Only the first scene error is reported

**Symptom:** fixing one `SceneError` reveals the next, one per run.

**Cause:** `parseScene` (and so `createGame`) throws for the first issue only. Also, the cross-field checks (duplicate ids, unknown prefabs, entities with nothing to draw or simulate) run only after every field passes.

**Fix:** to list everything, `SceneSchema.safeParse(json)` and print each `error.issues[i]` with `formatPath(issue.path)` ([api-reference.md](api-reference.md#validating-scenes); `apps/pebble-garden/src/garden/validate.ts`, lines 73-81). Expect a second round of cross-field issues once the field errors are fixed.

## The shot stateHash never changes

**Symptom:** every `pnpm shot` sidecar has the same `stateHash`, whatever the tick or input.

**Cause:** the game runs in worlds it creates itself, while `__pebble3d.stateHash` still reports `createGame`'s world, which holds no moving bodies.

**Fix:** override it after `createGame`: `Object.assign(window.__pebble3d ?? {}, { stateHash: () => myWorld.stateHash() })` (`apps/ringout/src/main.ts`, lines 95-99; `apps/pebble-garden/src/main.ts`, lines 182-186).

## biome --unsafe removed !important

**Symptom:** after `npx biome check --write --unsafe`, a CSS rule lost its `!important` and a hidden panel shows again.

**Cause:** biome's recommended rule `lint/complexity/noImportantStyles` has an unsafe fix that deletes `!important`. `--write` alone only reports it.

**Fix:** don't run `--unsafe` over CSS. Where `!important` is needed, keep it with a suppression comment on the line before: `/* biome-ignore lint/complexity/noImportantStyles: <reason> */` (`apps/pebble-garden/src/ui/hud.css`, lines 62-65), or raise the selector's specificity instead (`apps/drift-drone/src/game/ui/hud.css`, line 42).

## Fixed-mode captures with a worker sim

**Symptom:** with the sim in a Web Worker, `pnpm shot --ticks n` captures a different tick each run, or times out waiting for `__pebble3d.done`.

**Cause:** a worker steps on its own clock, so "one tick per frame, stop at n" cannot be enforced across the thread boundary.

**Fix:** run the same sim inline on the main thread whenever `mode` is `fixed` and use the worker only in realtime (`apps/swarm-siege/src/main.ts`, line 81 and lines 133-135; `apps/breakpoint/src/main.ts`, line 85). See [cookbook/instanced-crowds-and-perf.md](cookbook/instanced-crowds-and-perf.md).

## fps from a headless or WebGL run is misleading

**Symptom:** a game "holds 60 fps" in one measurement and stutters for a player, or a bench reports a few fps on a machine with a good GPU.

**Cause:**
- Headless Chromium without GPU flags renders WebGL on SwiftShader, a CPU rasteriser. Any fps measured there says nothing about the GPU path. `pnpm shot` refuses that adapter; a hand-written Playwright script or bench does not.
- WebGL can be several times slower than WebGPU for the same scene, so a number from one backend does not carry over to the other. Players on Firefox, Safari or a Chromium without WebGPU get WebGL.

**Fix:**
- Launch Chromium with `--use-angle=vulkan --enable-features=Vulkan --ignore-gpu-blocklist` (plus `--enable-unsafe-webgpu` for WebGPU), as `scripts/shot/shot.mjs` does.
- Confirm the renderer string names the real GPU before trusting a number: the sidecar's `adapterInfo`, or in the page `gl.getParameter(gl.getExtension("WEBGL_debug_renderer_info").UNMASKED_RENDERER_WEBGL)` on a WebGL context. "SwiftShader" or "llvmpipe" means software.
- Measure both backends (`?backend=webgpu` and `?backend=webgl`) on an idle GPU before calling a game smooth. See [fps numbers are low or noisy](#fps-numbers-are-low-or-noisy).

## Parameter properties fail in a Node script

**Symptom:** a headless script or CLI run with `node --experimental-strip-types` (or plain `node` on a version that strips types by default) fails with `SyntaxError [ERR_UNSUPPORTED_TYPESCRIPT_SYNTAX]: TypeScript parameter property is not supported in strip-only mode`, while vitest and Vite accept the same file.

**Cause:** Node's type stripping only removes type annotations; it does not transform TypeScript-only syntax. A constructor parameter property (`constructor(private readonly sim: MySim) {}`) needs a transform, and so do `enum` and `namespace`. vitest and Vite compile TypeScript fully, so the error appears only in the Node path.

**Fix:** in code a Node script imports (the sim, the bot, level loaders), declare the field and assign it in the constructor: `private readonly sim: MySim; constructor(sim: MySim) { this.sim = sim; }`. Use `as const` objects instead of `enum`. Or run that code through vitest instead of a bare `node` script.

## A night scene is too bright

**Symptom:** a night or interior scene still looks like daylight even with a dim sun, and the scene JSON has no field for point lights or environment strength.

**Cause:** the schema's `lighting` has only `sun`; the `studio` and `outdoor` presets also light every mesh with an environment map at full strength, which dominates once the sun is dim.

**Fix:** after boot, lower `renderer.three.scene.environmentIntensity` (Lanternfall uses 0.06, Breakpoint 0.42, Chain Reaction 0.55) and add three.js lights to `renderer.three.scene` yourself. Keep a small fixed pool of `PointLight`s with `castShadow = false` and move or re-colour them each frame rather than adding and removing lights, since a change in light count can force material recompiles (`LIGHT_POOL` in `apps/lanternfall/src/view/present.ts`).

## Draw calls climb with each character

**Symptom:** a handful of skinned glTF characters adds dozens of draw calls, and fps drops long before the triangle count looks large.

**Cause:** every shadow-casting mesh is drawn once in the main pass and once more for each shadow cascade (`CSM_CASCADES`, 3, in `packages/renderer/src/defaults/lighting.ts`). A character made of several skinned meshes multiplies that again.

**Fix:** turn off shadows for things that do not need them: `"castShadow": false` on the entity in the scene, or `mesh.castShadow = false` on meshes you add (small props, distant crowds, decals). Merge a character's meshes when the asset allows it, and watch `drawCalls` in `stats()` (or the overlay, toggled with the backtick key) as you add characters. More: [cookbook/instanced-crowds-and-perf.md](cookbook/instanced-crowds-and-perf.md).

## Decals on a splat floor get ink outlines

**Symptom:** with `post.style: "toon"`, a flat mesh lying on a Gaussian-splat floor (a puddle, a scorch mark, a target ring) gets a dark ink line around its edge.

**Cause:** the outline pass reads a mesh-only depth/normal prepass. The splat floor is not in it, so at the decal's edge the prepass sees a depth step from the decal to empty background and draws ink. There is no per-object outline opt-out.

**Fix:** make decals transparent materials (`transparent: true`, even at full opacity): transparent meshes are left out of the prepass and get no lines. See [cookbook/post-and-toon-style.md](cookbook/post-and-toon-style.md).

## A copied fps bench measures the wrong thing

**Symptom:** a `bench/fps.mjs` copied from another game times out, measures a title screen, or reports numbers that do not change with your scene.

**Cause:** each game's bench hard-codes its own preview port, URL params (seed, wave, level) and the phases it waits for. Rockfall's, for example, uses port 5242 and opens a fixed wave with rubble.

**Fix:** after copying, change the port to one your app does not use, the query string to one your `?demo=1` bot understands, and every phase name or probe it polls on `__pebble3d.game`. Build first (`pnpm --filter <app> build`). Benches are listed in [verification.md](verification.md#benches-and-capture-scripts).


===== docs/cookbook/scene-basics.md =====

# Scene basics

Goal: a scene file with a floor, walls, static and dynamic props and a camera, that validates the first time.

```json
{
	"version": 1,
	"environment": { "preset": "studio", "ground": { "size": 30 } },
	"bounds": { "min": [-6, -6], "max": [6, 6], "height": 2 },
	"lighting": { "sun": { "direction": [0.4, 1, 0.3], "intensity": 3 } },
	"camera": { "controller": "orbit", "presets": { "hero": { "position": [0, 6, 12], "target": [0, 1, 0], "fov": 45 } } },
	"entities": [
		{ "id": "table", "mesh": { "primitive": "box", "material": { "color": "#6b4f3a" } }, "body": { "type": "static" }, "transform": { "position": [0, 0.5, 0], "scale": [3, 1, 1.5] } },
		{ "id": "crate", "mesh": { "primitive": "box" }, "body": { "mass": 2, "friction": 0.7 }, "transform": { "position": [0.4, 2.5, 0], "scale": [0.5, 0.5, 0.5] } },
		{ "id": "ball", "mesh": { "primitive": "sphere", "material": { "color": "#e8553a", "roughness": 0.3 } }, "body": { "restitution": 0.6 }, "transform": { "position": [-0.6, 3, 0] } },
		{ "id": "sign", "mesh": { "primitive": "cylinder" }, "transform": { "position": [4, 1, -4], "scale": [0.2, 2, 0.2] } }
	]
}
```

Load it in the playground: save it as `apps/playground/scenes/<name>.json` and open `/?scene=<name>&cam=hero`, or `pnpm shot --scene <name> --cam hero`.

| Gotcha | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| A mesh without `body` has no physics | `sign` above is visual only: nothing collides with it and raycasts miss it. Add `"body": { "type": "static" }` for a solid prop. |
| `body` alone defaults to dynamic | `{}` is a dynamic body with friction 0.5, restitution 0, mass from volume at density 1. |
| Primitives are unit-sized | Box 1x1x1, sphere diameter 1, cylinder and capsule diameter x by height y. `transform.scale` is the size in metres, and `collider: "auto"` fits it. |
| Rotations are quaternions | `[x, y, z, w]`; 90 degrees about Y is `[0, 0.7071, 0, 0.7071]`. |
| Objects are strict | An unknown key (`"colour"`, `"size"`) fails validation with its path, e.g. `SceneError: entities[1].mesh: Unrecognized key: "colour"`. |
| Ids are unique | A duplicate `id` is an error; `game.ids.get("crate")` maps it to the sim id. |
| `bounds` are invisible | Static walls on the XZ rectangle, from y = 0 to `height`. Their ids are `__bounds.<side>`. |
| Static colliders may overlap | Static bodies never collide with each other (Rapier skips fixed-fixed pairs), so a static pad sunk into the floor or two overlapping static boxes cost nothing and push nothing. |
| Thin colliders | A 0.02 m static box holds resting bodies fine, but a fast body can pass through a thin collider in one tick: give the fast body `"ccd": true`, or make the collider thicker. A target that rules only test by position (an `inZone` check) needs no `body` at all. |
| `environment.ground` vs a floor box | `ground` is an infinite static half-space at `ground.y` (friction 0.5, restitution 0, the body defaults); `size` only sizes the visible plane, so bodies never fall off its edge. A static box floor has edges and its own `friction`/`restitution`. Both are spawned by `expandScene`, so Node and the browser get the same floor either way. |
| Static visuals are placed once | The renderer places a `static` body's mesh from the state buffer on the first `renderer.sync` after it is added, then never touches it again (dynamic, kinematic and character visuals follow their slot every frame). `teleport` on a static body moves its collider but not its mesh: anything that moves must be `kinematic`. Code that reads or merges static meshes (baking a level into a few draw calls) must wait until after the first frame, when they have their final transforms. |
| Collider limits | `plane` only on static bodies; `trimesh` only on static or kinematic ones. |

Every field and default: [scene-reference.md](../scene-reference.md). Editor validation: set `"$schema"` to `packages/sdk/scene.schema.json` relative to the file.

See it in: [apps/playground/scenes/studio.json](../../apps/playground/scenes/studio.json) (primitives, materials, prefabs), [apps/chain-reaction/levels/base.json](../../apps/chain-reaction/levels/base.json) (a studio base scene), [apps/lanternfall/src/view/present.ts](../../apps/lanternfall/src/view/present.ts) (merging the static level meshes on the first frame, after their placement, lines 227-241).


===== docs/cookbook/prefabs-and-spawners.md =====

# Prefabs and spawners

Goal: define a prop once, place copies of it, and rain more of them in at a fixed rate, deterministically.

```json
{
	"version": 1,
	"environment": { "preset": "studio", "ground": {} },
	"sim": { "seed": 7 },
	"prefabs": {
		"crate": { "mesh": { "primitive": "box", "material": { "color": "#a8743f", "roughness": 0.78 } }, "transform": { "scale": [0.5, 0.5, 0.5] }, "body": { "friction": 0.7 } },
		"ball": { "mesh": { "primitive": "sphere", "material": { "color": "#3a7be8" } }, "transform": { "scale": [0.3, 0.3, 0.3] }, "body": { "restitution": 0.5 } }
	},
	"entities": [
		{ "id": "crate-1", "prefab": "crate", "transform": { "position": [0, 0.25, 0] } },
		{ "id": "crate-big", "prefab": "crate", "transform": { "position": [1.2, 0.5, 0], "scale": [1, 1, 1] } },
		{ "id": "rain", "spawner": { "prefab": "ball", "rate": 4, "count": 60, "area": { "min": [-2, 4, -2], "max": [2, 6, 2] } } }
	]
}
```

How it works:

- `prefab` is deep-merged under the entity: entity fields win, objects merge key by key (`crate-big` keeps the prefab's mesh and body and only changes `scale`).
- A spawner entity has only `spawner` (plus `id` and optional `transform`). The engine's Rust spawner creates `count` bodies, `rate` per second, uniformly inside `area`, from a seeded generator: `spawner.seed`, else `sim.seed` + the entity's index.
- `createGame` drains new bodies each frame (`world.drainSpawned()`, flat `(id, slot, spawnerSimId)` triples) and draws them. Dynamic primitive props, spawned or not, are instanced: one draw call per primitive + size + material.

| Gotcha | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Spawner entity is bare | A `mesh`, `body` or `character` on the spawner entity itself is an error: put them on the prefab. |
| Prefab must have a body | And no `character`; the error is on `entities[i].spawner.prefab`. |
| Spawned bodies are not in `game.ids` | Track them from `drainSpawned` in your own loop, or by slot. |
| Prefab `position` is ignored for spawns | They land in `area`; the prefab's rotation and scale apply. |
| Runtime spawners | `world.spawn('{"spawner":{"template":{...},"rate":..,"count":..,"areaMin":[..],"areaMax":[..],"seed":..}}')` works too, but then you drain and draw the bodies yourself; despawn the spawner entity once it is done. |
| Own world, own draining | With a custom boot (no `createGame`), check `world.spawnedPending() > 0` before `drainSpawned()` (it allocates). |

See it in: [apps/playground/scenes/showcase.json](../../apps/playground/scenes/showcase.json) (prefabs and the `ball-spawner`), [apps/rockfall/src/game/sim.ts](../../apps/rockfall/src/game/sim.ts) (runtime spawners from wave orders, lines 441-475; draining, lines 595-640), [apps/rockfall/src/game/view/rock-view.ts](../../apps/rockfall/src/game/view/rock-view.ts) (drawing drained bodies, lines 68-101).


===== docs/cookbook/bodies-impulses-velocity.md =====

# Bodies, impulses and velocity

Goal: push, launch, spin, move and spawn bodies from code, and read their position and velocity back, without allocating per frame.

```ts
import type { Game } from "@pebble3d/sdk/game";

const VEL = 12; // linearVelocity writes [vx, vy, vz] to scratch [12..15)

export function setup(game: Game) {
	const world = game.sim.world;
	const id = game.ids.get("crate");
	if (id === undefined) throw new Error('no "crate" in the scene');
	const slot = world.slotOf(id);

	world.applyImpulse(id, 0, 6, 0); // N·s: delta-v = impulse / mass
	world.applyTorqueImpulse(id, 0, 0.5, 0);

	// Spawn at runtime (EntityDescJson, camelCase). No visual is created for it.
	const rock = world.spawn(JSON.stringify({
		position: [0, 4, 0],
		body: { type: "dynamic", mass: 3, collider: { shape: "sphere", radius: 0.25 } },
	}));
	world.setVelocity(rock, 2, 0, 0, 0, 5, 0); // linear m/s, angular rad/s

	game.onFrame(() => {
		const v = game.views; // refreshed by createGame before onFrame
		const y = v.curr[slot * 8 + 1] as number;
		const asleep = ((v.curr[slot * 8 + 7] as number) & 2) !== 0;
		if (world.linearVelocity(id) && !asleep) {
			const vy = v.scratch[VEL + 1] as number;
			// fell off the world: snap back (NO_INTERP) with zero velocity
			if (y < -5 || vy < -30) world.teleport(id, 0, 2, 0);
		}
	});
}
```

| Gotcha | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Body type matters | `applyImpulse`, `applyTorqueImpulse`, `setVelocity` work on dynamic bodies only; `setKinematicPose` on kinematic only. They return `false` otherwise. |
| Mass | Default is collider volume at density 1. Scale impulses by mass for a target speed: `m * (target - v)` (Chain Reaction springs). |
| Torque is world-frame | `applyTorqueImpulse(id, tx, ty, tz)` takes a world-space angular impulse (N·m·s), not one in the body's local axes: the change in angular velocity is `I⁻¹ · τ` with the inertia tensor rotated to the body's current orientation. To spin about a body axis, rotate that axis into world space first (from the quaternion in `views.curr`). |
| Inertia follows the collider | The inertia tensor is the collider's shape at uniform density. With `mass` set, Rapier keeps the shape's tensor and scales it to that mass, so doubling `mass` halves the spin a torque impulse gives. A 2 x 1 x 0.5 m box of 1 kg yawed 90 degrees, given `applyTorqueImpulse(id, 1, 0, 0)`, spins at 2.4 rad/s (`1 / I_zz`, I_zz = m(2² + 1²)/12); at `mass: 10`, 0.24 rad/s. A sphere's inertia is the same about every axis (`0.4 m r²`), so its frame never matters. |
| Spheres roll forever | Rapier has no rolling resistance. A ball rolling on flat ground keeps its speed indefinitely with the default `angularDamping: 0` (a 0.5 m sphere set rolling at 3 m/s still does 3.0 m/s after 10 s). Give rolling bodies `"angularDamping"` (0.25 to 0.6 is typical; 0.5 brought that ball to 0.73 m/s after 10 s) and optionally a little `"linearDamping"`. Damping scales velocity by `1 / (1 + dt · damping)` each tick. |
| No contact events | The engine reports no collision or contact events. Detect hits in your rules after each `world.step`, from state you already read: the distance between two bodies dropping below the sum of their radii (and the closing speed along the line of centres), or a velocity change in one tick that gravity and your own impulses do not explain. Keep a per-pair "touching" flag so a contact fires once, not every tick. |
| Kinematic pose has no scale | `setKinematicPose` sets position and rotation only; a collider's size is fixed at spawn. To resize a body, `despawn` it and `spawn` a new one with the new collider (and resize its visual yourself); to make it vanish, `despawn` it. |
| Views go stale | `spawn` can grow wasm memory. Call `game.views.refresh()` after spawning, before reading `curr` or `scratch` in the same frame. |
| Spawned bodies are invisible | `world.spawn` creates physics only. Draw it with your own mesh read from its slot, or through `game.renderer.instances.add(key, geometry, material, slot)`. |
| Raycasts lag a tick | A body spawned this tick is not hit by raycasts until after the next `step`. |
| Free slots | `despawn(id)` frees the slot (flags read 0) and a later spawn may reuse it; drop your slot index too. |
| Determinism | Apply forces inside the tick (before `world.step`), from seeded values only, never from frame time. |

Full method list and return values: [api-reference.md](../api-reference.md#body-control).

See it in: [apps/chain-reaction/src/puzzle/sim.ts](../../apps/chain-reaction/src/puzzle/sim.ts) (spring and fan impulses, lines 217-260; velocity reads, lines 266-293), [apps/katana-defense/src/game/view/zombie-view.ts](../../apps/katana-defense/src/game/view/zombie-view.ts) (spawn a ragdoll capsule and `setVelocity`, lines 496-537), [apps/field-notes/src/main.ts](../../apps/field-notes/src/main.ts) (`teleport` on restart, lines 158-166), [apps/ringout/src/game/sim.ts](../../apps/ringout/src/game/sim.ts) (rolling torque about the travel axis, lines 210-212; impacts from distance and closing speed, lines 341-404), [apps/drift-drone/src/game/sim.ts](../../apps/drift-drone/src/game/sim.ts) (crashes from the velocity the drone would have had with no contact, lines 407-423 and 441-451), [apps/pebble-garden/src/garden/sim.ts](../../apps/pebble-garden/src/garden/sim.ts) (impact sounds from a one-tick velocity change, lines 240-263), [apps/pebble-garden/src/garden/pieces.ts](../../apps/pebble-garden/src/garden/pieces.ts) (a rolling pebble with `angularDamping`, lines 156-163).


===== docs/cookbook/raycasts.md =====

# Raycasts

Goal: ground probes, line-of-sight tests and "what did I hit" queries against the physics world.

```ts
import type { Game } from "@pebble3d/sdk/game";

const RAY_ALL = 0;
const RAY_STATIC = 1; // ground, bounds, static entities only
const RAY_EXCLUDE = 2; // everything but `excludeId`

/** Height of the ground under (x, z), or 0 when nothing is below. */
export function groundY(game: Game, x: number, z: number, selfId: number): number {
	const top = 20;
	const world = game.sim.world;
	if (!world.raycast(x, top, z, 0, -1, 0, top + 5, RAY_EXCLUDE, selfId)) return 0;
	return top - (game.views.scratch[0] as number); // scratch [toi, nx, ny, nz, id]
}

/** True when a static collider blocks the segment from a to b. */
export function blocked(game: Game, a: number[], b: number[]): boolean {
	const dx = b[0] - a[0], dy = b[1] - a[1], dz = b[2] - a[2];
	const len = Math.hypot(dx, dy, dz);
	return game.sim.world.raycast(a[0], a[1], a[2], dx, dy, dz, len, RAY_STATIC, 0);
}

/** Scene id of the first body hit, or null. `byId` is game.ids inverted once at startup. */
export function pick(game: Game, byId: Map<number, string>, o: number[], d: number[]): string | null {
	if (!game.sim.world.raycast(o[0], o[1], o[2], d[0], d[1], d[2], 100, RAY_ALL, 0)) return null;
	return byId.get(game.views.scratch[4] as number) ?? null;
}
```

| Gotcha | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Results live in scratch | `raycast` returns a boolean; the hit is in `game.views.scratch[0..5)`. Read it before the next query (any query overwrites scratch). |
| Direction need not be unit | The engine normalises it, so `toi` is metres and `maxToi` is a distance. |
| Exclude the caster | A probe from inside a body hits that body first; use filter 2 with its id. |
| Spawned this tick = invisible | Queries see the broad phase as of the last `step`. |
| Hit id 1 is usually `__ground` | Generated statics (`__ground`, `__bounds.<side>`) are in `game.ids`. Filter 1 still hits the invisible bounds walls; Field Notes skips them by id for its camera arm. |
| Views after spawning | If you spawned this frame, `game.views.refresh()` first; a stale view reads detached memory. |

Filters and the scratch layout: [api-reference.md](../api-reference.md#raycasts).

See it in: [apps/rockfall/src/game/sim.ts](../../apps/rockfall/src/game/sim.ts) (pickup resting height with filter 2, lines 934-951), [apps/ghostline/src/game/sim.ts](../../apps/ghostline/src/game/sim.ts) (marble ground normal from scratch `[1..4)`, lines 359-391), [apps/field-notes/src/game/present.ts](../../apps/field-notes/src/game/present.ts) (camera arm that ignores the bounds walls, lines 94-105), [apps/rockfall/src/game/view/telegraph-view.ts](../../apps/rockfall/src/game/view/telegraph-view.ts) (landing-ring height under each falling rock, the rock excluded, lines 112-116).


===== docs/cookbook/character-and-camera.md =====

# Character and camera

Goal: a walking, jumping player with a third-person camera, eased acceleration and animation clips matched to its speed.

```json
{
	"version": 1,
	"environment": { "preset": "studio", "ground": {} },
	"camera": { "controller": "thirdPerson", "presets": { "hero": { "position": [6, 4, 8], "target": [0, 1, 0] } } },
	"entities": [
		{
			"id": "player",
			"mesh": { "primitive": "capsule", "material": { "color": "#4a8fe0" } },
			"body": {},
			"character": { "speed": 4, "sprintSpeed": 6.5, "jumpSpeed": 5.5, "accel": 14 },
			"transform": { "position": [0, 1, 0], "scale": [0.6, 1.8, 0.6] }
		},
		{ "id": "step", "mesh": { "primitive": "box" }, "body": { "type": "static" }, "transform": { "position": [2, 0.15, 0], "scale": [1, 0.3, 1] } }
	]
}
```

`createGame` turns the first entity with a `character` into `game.player`: WASD/arrows move relative to the camera yaw, Space jumps, Shift sprints, and a click pointer-locks the mouse for the camera. A glTF character instead uses an explicit capsule collider and maps clips, as in `apps/field-notes/scenes/yard.json`:

```json
{ "gltf": { "url": "/assets/rocketbox-male-adult-16.glb", "animations": { "idle": "Idle", "walk": { "clip": "Walk", "speed": 0.979 }, "run": { "clip": "Run", "speed": 5.649 }, "jump": "Jump", "fall": "Fall" } } }
```

(a fragment: the value of `mesh`; pair it with `"body": { "type": "kinematic", "collider": { "shape": "capsule", "halfHeight": 0.5, "radius": 0.3 } }`).

| Gotcha | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Body is required | `character` needs a kinematic body with a capsule collider. `"body": {}` defaults to kinematic for a character; `collider: "auto"` on a glTF makes a hull, which is rejected, so give the capsule. |
| Capsule auto-fit | On a capsule primitive, `scale.y` must exceed `scale.x` (it is the total height). |
| `accel` | m/s² toward the input velocity; 0 (default) is instant. 14 ramps a 4 m/s walk in about 0.3 s. |
| Clip `speed` | The clip's authored ground speed; playback rate becomes `speed / authored`, clamped to 0.6-1.6, which stops foot sliding. Walk/run switch at 0.75 x `sprintSpeed`. |
| Driving it from code | Write `game.player.input` (`keys.f/b/l/r`, `jump`, `sprint`). It is sent as `setCharacterInput` before your `onFrame` runs, so a value set in the frame at tick t is first used by the step that produces tick t + 2. |
| Your own `setCharacterInput` for the player | `createGame` calls `setCharacterInput` for `game.player` from `game.player.input` every frame, **including frames that advance 0 ticks** (any display above 60 Hz, where most frames run no tick). If your rules call `world.setCharacterInput(game.player.simId, ...)` themselves only inside the per-tick loop, the rig overwrites that on the next 0-tick frame and the following `world.step` uses keyboard input instead (a demo bot that stops steering, a player who walks on the title screen). Re-send your intent at the end of every `onFrame`, after the tick loop: it then always wins. Or drive the player only through `game.player.input`. |
| Which character is the player | The first entity in `entities` (after prefab expansion) that has a `character`. Reorder the entities to change it; there is no option to pick another or to have none while keeping characters. |
| More characters | Only the player gets an animated `CharacterView`. Every other character is still moved by the renderer (its root follows its capsule), but plays no clip and never turns until you call `game.renderer.attachCharacter(simId, clipMap)` once, then each frame `world.characterState(simId)` and `view.update(frame, dt)` with `{ grounded, vx, vz, vy, sprintSpeed }` read from scratch `[8..12)`. `update` also turns the model toward its velocity; set `view.root.rotation` after it to face elsewhere. |
| Reading it back | `world.characterState(id)` writes `[grounded, vx, vz, vy]` to scratch `[8..12)` (vz before vy). |
| Camera | `game.player.camera` (`ThirdPersonController`): `yaw` (0 looks down -Z), `pitch` (-1.2 to 0.3), `distance`. Its arm ray is static-only. `game.setCamera("hero")` suspends it; `"controller"` resumes it. Your own camera instead: [custom-camera.md](custom-camera.md). |
| Moving platforms | Set `"ridePlatforms": true` on the `character` to stand on a kinematic body driven by `world.setKinematicPose` each tick: the character moves (and turns about the platform's origin) exactly with it, and keeps its velocity as momentum after a jump or walking off. Without the flag Rapier's own platform friction lags a tick and a character at rest on a kinematic body can get pinned and fail to walk. The reported `characterState` velocity stays the character's own, relative to the platform. Set the platform's pose before the `world.step` it should apply to. A pose jump over 1 m in one tick counts as a teleport and is not carried. While riding, steps up to `stepHeight` are climbed by a lift-and-set-down cast, which ignores autostep's `min_width`. |
| Own character | A character spawned with `world.spawn` (no `createGame` rig) is driven only by your `setCharacterInput` calls each tick. |

See it in: [apps/field-notes/scenes/yard.json](../../apps/field-notes/scenes/yard.json) (glTF player with `accel`, lines 65-100), [apps/field-notes/src/main.ts](../../apps/field-notes/src/main.ts) (a sim writing `rig.input` from its own buttons, lines 210-218), [apps/playground/src/main.ts](../../apps/playground/src/main.ts) (scripted input and the jump timing, lines 132-179), [apps/rockfall/src/game/sim.ts](../../apps/rockfall/src/game/sim.ts) (character spawned from JSON and driven per tick, lines 264-287 and 373-415), [apps/lanternfall/src/main.ts](../../apps/lanternfall/src/main.ts) (re-sending the sim's intents after every frame's ticks, lines 82-91) with [apps/lanternfall/src/game/sim.ts](../../apps/lanternfall/src/game/sim.ts) (`assertInput`, lines 403-420), [apps/lanternfall/src/view/present.ts](../../apps/lanternfall/src/view/present.ts) (guards animated with `attachCharacter`, lines 155-160 and 248-260), [apps/skyrun/src/game/sim.ts](../../apps/skyrun/src/game/sim.ts) (a runner with `ridePlatforms` on kinematic movers, lines 169 and 206).


===== docs/cookbook/splat-environments.md =====

# Splat environments

Goal: use a Gaussian-splat capture as the world, lit by itself, with mesh shadows on its floor and invisible colliders where its walls are.

```json
{
	"version": 1,
	"environment": {
		"preset": "outdoor",
		"hdri": "/assets/qwantani_noon_puresky_2k.hdr",
		"fog": false,
		"splat": {
			"url": "/assets/knock-community-hall-800k.spz",
			"position": [0, -1.006, 0],
			"rotation": [0.99997, -0.0006, 7e-5, -0.0077],
			"scale": 2.2,
			"envFromSplat": true,
			"floorY": 0,
			"exposure": 0.88,
			"saturation": 1.1
		},
		"ground": { "y": 0, "size": 80, "visible": false }
	},
	"bounds": { "min": [-6, 7.2], "max": [12.5, 14.2], "height": 4 },
	"post": { "toneMapping": "aces" },
	"entities": [
		{ "id": "planter", "body": { "type": "static", "collider": { "shape": "box", "halfExtents": [0.6, 0.4, 0.6] } }, "transform": { "position": [3, 0.4, 10] } }
	]
}
```

The splat and HDRI come from `pnpm fetch-assets` (served at `/assets/`). Try it: `pnpm shot --scene showcase --cam hero`.

| Gotcha | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Splats have no physics | Add an invisible `ground` (`visible: false`) at the capture floor, `bounds` for its edges and body-only static entities (no `mesh`) for furniture. |
| Align the floor first | Tune `position`/`rotation`/`scale` until the capture floor sits at y = 0, then set `floorY` to it: the invisible shadow catcher goes there and depth of field uses it for ground splats. Field Notes' `?scout=<scene>&pose=...` renders a 1 m grid over the splat for this. |
| Splats neither cast nor receive shadows | Only meshes cast, onto the shadow catcher. |
| `envFromSplat` | Lights meshes from a cube capture of the splat (once, at load) instead of the HDRI; the background stays. |
| Colour | `exposure` and `saturation` compensate the tone mapper; `renderer.splatColor` (`exposure`, `saturation`, `tint`) changes them live, for example a dusk grade. |
| Formats | `.spz`, `.ply`, `.splat`, `.ksplat`, picked by extension. |
| Budget | Above 1,500,000 splats the renderer logs a `console.warn`, which fails `pnpm shot`. Decimate first (the manifest's `derive` step runs `splat-transform`). |
| Missing file | A failed load is reported once as a console error and the game runs without the splat (`showcase-badsplat.json` tests this); `pnpm shot` then fails unless you pass `--allow-console-error`. |

See it in: [apps/playground/scenes/showcase.json](../../apps/playground/scenes/showcase.json), [apps/field-notes/scenes/courtyard.json](../../apps/field-notes/scenes/courtyard.json) (an interior capture), [apps/field-notes/src/main.ts](../../apps/field-notes/src/main.ts) (obstacles injected as static boxes, lines 75-98), [apps/field-notes/src/scout.ts](../../apps/field-notes/src/scout.ts) (alignment grid), [apps/katana-defense/src/game/view/dusk.ts](../../apps/katana-defense/src/game/view/dusk.ts) (live `splatColor` grade, lines 136-145).


===== docs/cookbook/post-and-toon-style.md =====

# Post-processing and the toon style

Goal: tune exposure, tone mapping, bloom and AO, or switch the whole scene to the opt-in cel-shaded look with ink outlines.

```json
{
	"version": 1,
	"environment": { "preset": "studio", "ground": {} },
	"post": {
		"exposure": 1,
		"toneMapping": "aces",
		"bloom": { "enabled": true, "strength": 0.45, "threshold": 1.4 },
		"ao": { "enabled": true, "radius": 0.5 },
		"style": "toon",
		"toon": {
			"bands": 3,
			"shadowTone": 0.22,
			"rim": 0.6,
			"specular": 0.7,
			"outline": { "width": 1.5, "color": "#1a1418" },
			"splat": { "levels": 3, "saturation": 1.3 }
		}
	},
	"entities": [
		{ "id": "ball", "mesh": { "primitive": "sphere", "material": { "color": "#e8553a" } }, "body": {}, "transform": { "position": [0, 2, 0] } }
	]
}
```

`post.style` defaults to `"pbr"`, which ignores `post.toon`. With `"toon"`, scene entities and their glTFs are converted by the renderer. Objects your code builds are not:

```ts
import { ToonNodeMaterial } from "@pebble3d/renderer";

const gltf = await game.renderer.loadGltf(url);
game.renderer.stylize(gltf.scene); // once, on the cached scene, before any clone (no-op in pbr)
const steel = new ToonNodeMaterial({ metalness: 0.85, roughness: 0.22 });
steel.toonRim = 1.5; // multiplies post.toon.rim for this material
steel.toonSpecular = 1.6; // multiplies post.toon.specular
```

| Gotcha | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Opt-in | Leave `style` unset for PBR. Existing scenes must not change look, so never flip a default. |
| Bloom threshold is HDR luminance | The default 2 catches only highlights and emissives; lower it (1.0-1.4) for a softer glow. |
| Outlines come from meshes | The ink pass reads a mesh-only depth/normal prepass: splats and transparent meshes get no lines. |
| Splats are graded, not shaded | `toon.splat` posterises the capture's lightness into `levels` and tints shadows/highlights. |
| One toon style per page | The toon parameters are page-global uniforms (`TOON`); a second renderer overwrites them. `setToonUniforms(settings)` changes them live. |
| Check `renderer.style` | `"toon"` or `"pbr"`; shared code can branch on it. `stylize` is safe to call in either. |
| Exposure at runtime | `game.renderer.three.renderer.toneMappingExposure` (Field Notes' photo EV, Ronin Outpost's dusk). |

Every field and range: [scene-reference.md](../scene-reference.md#post). Look at the result: `pnpm shot --scene showcase-toon --cam hero`.

See it in: [apps/katana-defense/scenes/arena.json](../../apps/katana-defense/scenes/arena.json) (toon post, lines 31-52), [apps/katana-defense/src/main.ts](../../apps/katana-defense/src/main.ts) (`stylize` on cached glTFs, lines 120-127), [apps/katana-defense/src/game/view/katana.ts](../../apps/katana-defense/src/game/view/katana.ts) (`ToonNodeMaterial` with rim and specular multipliers, lines 76-88), [apps/playground/scenes/showcase-toon.json](../../apps/playground/scenes/showcase-toon.json).


===== docs/cookbook/depth-of-field.md =====

# Depth of field

Goal: a photo-mode blur with a focus distance you control, that also works on splat captures.

Depth of field is a renderer control, not a scene field: `game.renderer.dof` (`DepthOfFieldControls`). It is off by default and costs nothing until first enabled.

```ts
// Defaults (DOF_DEFAULTS in @pebble3d/renderer): focus 5, range 3, bokeh 1, backdrop 30.
const dof = game.renderer.dof;
dof.bokeh.value = 1.1; // bokeh size, unitless
dof.backdrop.value = 30; // metres assumed for depthless pixels that miss the floor (sky, far walls)

let photoMode = false;
window.addEventListener("keydown", (e) => {
	if (e.code === "KeyF") photoMode = !photoMode;
});

game.onFrame(() => {
	dof.enabled = photoMode;
	if (!photoMode) return;
	const focus = distanceToSubject(); // metres along the view direction
	dof.focus.value = focus;
	dof.range.value = Math.min(8, Math.max(0.35, focus * 0.42)); // metres to full blur
});
```

| Gotcha | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| First enable builds the chain | The DOF passes are built the first time `enabled` turns true, so that frame does extra work; enable it once early (as a warm-up) if a hitch matters. Toggling afterwards only swaps the pipeline output. |
| Values are uniforms | Set `focus.value`, `range.value`, `bokeh.value`, `backdrop.value`, never replace the objects. |
| Focus is view depth | Distance along the camera's forward axis, not the straight-line distance to the subject (they differ off-centre). |
| Splats have no depth | A pixel with no mesh depth gets a proxy: where its view ray hits the plane at `environment.splat.floorY`, that distance; otherwise `backdrop`. Set `floorY` correctly or ground splats blur wrongly. |
| Transparent meshes blur like the backdrop | Additive glows and particles write no depth, so they take the proxy distance of what is behind them even when they sit in focus. |
| Tie `range` to the lens | Field Notes uses `focus * 0.42 * (40 / fovDeg)`, clamped to 0.35-8 m: the blur ramp grows with focus distance and with zoom. |

See it in: [apps/field-notes/src/game/present.ts](../../apps/field-notes/src/game/present.ts) (`bokeh`/`backdrop` per site, lines 115-117; enable while the camera is raised and drive focus and range, lines 280-290). The controls and defaults are in [api-reference.md](../api-reference.md) (`DepthOfFieldControls`, `DOF_DEFAULTS`).


===== docs/cookbook/deterministic-game-loop.md =====

# Deterministic game loop: input log, replay, ghosts

Goal: game rules that advance once per 60 Hz tick from a logged input, so a run replays bit-exactly, can be verified headless, and can race a ghost.

The pattern of Ghostline, Chain Reaction and Breakpoint: the game sim owns its `World`s and steps them itself, and `createGame` only renders. (Rockfall does the same without `createGame`; Ronin Outpost's sim is plain JS with the same loop.) The sim reads one input record per tick and nothing else: no DOM, no `Math.random`, no `Date`, no frame time.

```ts
import type { SimHandle } from "@pebble3d/sdk/sim";
import { InputLog, type TickInput } from "./input.ts"; // copy apps/ghostline/src/game/input.ts
type World = SimHandle["world"];
const DT = 1 / 60;
class MySim {
	tick = 0;
	readonly world: World;
	constructor(host: { create(seed: number, g: number): World }, readonly seed: number) {
		this.world = host.create(seed, -9.81); // spawn bodies here, from seeded values only
	}
	step(i: TickInput): void { /* apply i to bodies */ this.world.step(1); this.tick++; }
	hash(): string { return this.world.stateHash(); } // 16 hex chars
	free(): void { this.world.free(); } // every World holds wasm memory
}

// More worlds from the module createGame loaded (apps/ghostline/src/game/physics.ts).
const Ctor = game.sim.world.constructor as new (seed: number, g: number) => World;
const host = { create: (s: number, g: number) => new Ctor(s, g) };
const sim = new MySim(host, seed);
const ghost = best ? new MySim(host, best.seed) : null; // best: { seed, log: InputLog, hash }
const log = new InputLog(); // 3 bytes per tick, grows by doubling
const input: TickInput = { x: 0, z: 0, buttons: 0 }, ghostInput = { ...input }; // x, z: int8
let acc = 0;
game.onFrame((dt) => {
	acc += dt;
	let n = 0;
	for (; acc >= DT - 1e-9 && n < 5; n++) {
		acc -= DT;
		sampleInto(input); // live input or bot.next(input): the same type
		log.push(input);
		sim.step(input);
		if (ghost && ghost.tick < best.log.length) ghost.step(best.log.read(ghost.tick, ghostInput));
	}
	if (n === 5) acc = 0; // fell behind: drop time instead of spiralling
	present(Math.min(1, acc / DT)); // interpolate visuals between ticks
});

/** Replay = a fresh world, the same seed, the same inputs; then compare hashes. */
function verify(seed: number, l: InputLog, expected: string): boolean {
	const s = new MySim(host, seed);
	try { for (let t = 0; t < l.length; t++) s.step(l.read(t, ghostInput)); return s.hash() === expected; }
	finally { s.free(); }
}
```

| Gotcha | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Tick order | Here the sim owns the world: `step()` applies the input, then calls `world.step(1)` (rules, then physics), and nothing else steps that world. `verify` and any Node test call the same `step()`, so the order matches by construction. This differs from the `createGame`-steps-physics pattern in [getting-started.md](../getting-started.md#tick-order) (physics, then rules in `onFrame`); a headless verifier must copy whichever order the browser path uses, ideally by calling the same function. Do not mix them: a sim that calls `world.step` itself must run on its own world, not on `game.sim.world`, which `createGame` already steps. |
| Quantise before logging | Store int8 axes (`Math.round(v * 127)`) and feed the sim the same quantised value live and in replay; a float that differs in the last bit diverges. |
| Ghosts re-simulate | A ghost is a second world fed the logged inputs in lockstep, not recorded positions. Fingerprint the course and rules into the record and discard stale ones. |
| One hash per run | Save `{ seed, inputs, hash }`; `verify` proves the run. Mix game state into it (score, hp) to catch rule drift. `free()` every world on restart. In fixed mode `dt` is exactly 1/60, so one tick runs per frame. |
| The `deterministic` build | Bit-identical across runs and between Node and Chromium; `fast` only for the same binary on the same machine. Your own JS math (`Math.sin`...) can still differ between JS engines: Ghostline reports a diverged ghost instead of trusting it. |

See it in: [apps/ghostline/src/game/ghost.ts](../../apps/ghostline/src/game/ghost.ts) (ghost record, re-simulation and `verifyRecord`, lines 136-212), [apps/ghostline/src/game/app.ts](../../apps/ghostline/src/game/app.ts) (live run and ghost per tick, lines 463-477; accumulator, lines 559-577), [apps/ghostline/src/game/input.ts](../../apps/ghostline/src/game/input.ts) (int8 `InputLog`, three bytes per tick, serialised as run-length encoded base64), [apps/rockfall/src/game/input.ts](../../apps/rockfall/src/game/input.ts), [apps/rockfall/src/game/rng.ts](../../apps/rockfall/src/game/rng.ts) (seeded mulberry32), [apps/breakpoint/src/game/replay.ts](../../apps/breakpoint/src/game/replay.ts) (instant replay by re-simulation). Testing it: [verification.md](../verification.md#determinism).


===== docs/cookbook/demo-bot-and-captures.md =====

# Demo bot and captures

Goal: a `?demo=1` autoplayer that plays the whole loop, and a script of reproducible screenshots driven by it.

```ts
/** `?demo=1` autoplayer. Reads only sim state and writes the same TickInput a player does. */
export class DemoBot {
	private t = 0;
	current = "start"; // what it is doing, exposed as a probe
	constructor(private readonly sim: MySim) {}

	next(out: TickInput): void {
		this.t++;
		out.buttons = 0;
		out.x = 0;
		out.z = 0;
		if (this.sim.phase === "title") {
			if (this.t > 90) out.buttons = BTN.START; // hold the title for 1.5 s
			this.current = "title";
			return;
		}
		const g = this.sim.nearestGoal(); // deterministic choice from sim state
		out.x = Math.round(Math.sign(g.x - this.sim.px) * 127);
		out.z = Math.round(Math.sign(g.z - this.sim.pz) * 127);
		this.current = "seek";
	}
}

// main.ts: one input source per tick, chosen once.
const bot = q.get("demo") === "1" ? new DemoBot(sim) : null;
// in the tick loop: if (bot) bot.next(input); else live.sample(input);
Object.assign(window.__pebble3d ?? {}, { game: { phase: () => sim.phase, bot: () => bot?.current ?? null } });
```

Capture script (`apps/<app>/bench/capture-final.sh`, after `apps/rockfall/bench/capture-final.sh`):

```bash
pnpm --filter my-game build >/dev/null
shot() { local name=$1; shift
	node scripts/shot/shot.mjs --app my-game --no-build --out artifacts/games/my-game --name "$name" "$@"; }
shot 01-title --ticks 240
shot 02-mid-run --ticks 1800 --param demo=1 --param seed=7
shot 03-loop --ticks 1200 --sequence 90:3 --scale 0.6 --no-frames --param demo=1 --param seed=7
```

| Gotcha | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Same input type as a player | The bot must go through `TickInput`, never poke sim fields, so it tests the real path and its runs replay. |
| No randomness of its own | Draw from sim state or a seeded `Rng`. Then a capture at tick n is the same frame every run. |
| Fix the seed in fixed mode | Games default to a fixed seed when `mode=fixed` (Rockfall 7, Field Notes 23) and pass `--param seed=` explicitly in scripts. |
| Scout ticks headless | Run the same sim in Node, in the browser's tick order, until the event (a goal, the result screen) and note the engine tick: `for (t = 0; t < max && !done(); t++) { world.step(1); views.refresh(); bot.next(sim, input); sim.step(input); }` leaves `world.tick()` at the event tick for a `createGame` app. `--ticks n` captures right after engine tick n, so pass the event tick plus how long the result should be visible (e.g. +30 for 0.5 s). Pin it in a test (`expect(eventTick).toBe(...)`) so a rule change that moves it fails loudly. Loop setup: [getting-started.md](../getting-started.md#tests-in-node). |
| Read `mode` and `ticks` | Without them the shot never sees `__pebble3d.done` and times out. |
| Mute in fixed mode | Audio stays off for captures (see [audio-sfx.md](audio-sfx.md)). |
| Look at every PNG | Exit 0 only means no console errors. |

See it in: [apps/rockfall/src/game/bot.ts](../../apps/rockfall/src/game/bot.ts) (threat-scoring dodger), [apps/chain-reaction/src/demo.ts](../../apps/chain-reaction/src/demo.ts) (scripted placement then run), [apps/rockfall/bench/capture-final.sh](../../apps/rockfall/bench/capture-final.sh). Every game's bot: [verification.md](../verification.md#demo-bots).


===== docs/cookbook/instanced-crowds-and-perf.md =====

# Instanced crowds and performance

Goal: hundreds of bodies or characters at 60 fps on a laptop GPU.

Scene props are instanced for you: every dynamic primitive entity (and every spawned body) with the same primitive, size, material and `castShadow` shares one `InstancedMesh`. For bodies your code spawns, add them to the same registry by slot; `createGame`'s `renderer.sync` moves them every frame:

```ts
import { BoxGeometry, Color, MeshStandardNodeMaterial } from "three/webgpu";

const geo = new BoxGeometry(0.5, 0.5, 0.5);
const mat = new MeshStandardNodeMaterial({ roughness: 0.8 });
const tint = new Color();
const inst = game.renderer.instances; // InstanceRegistry

function addRock(id: number, shade: number): void {
	const slot = game.sim.world.slotOf(id);
	inst.add("rock|0", geo, mat, slot, tint.setRGB(shade, shade, shade)); // one draw call per key
}
function removeRock(id: number, slot: number): void {
	inst.removeSlot(slot); // before (or right after) world.despawn(id)
	game.sim.world.despawn(id);
}
// Tiny things skip the shadow cascades. The mesh is replaced when its group grows
// (castShadow carries over): look it up with mesh(key), don't keep the reference.
const pebbles = inst.mesh("pebble|0");
if (pebbles) pebbles.castShadow = false;
```

| Technique | Where |
| --- | --- |
| Skinned crowd: clone every avatar up front (`SkeletonUtils.clone`) into a pool sized for the worst wave; never clone mid-fight. | `apps/katana-defense/src/game/view/zombie-pool.ts` (pool sizes), `zombie-view.ts` (clones) |
| Blob shadows: one instanced, depth-write-off quad per zombie instead of shadow-casting skinned meshes. | `apps/katana-defense/src/game/view/zombie-view.ts`, lines 81-99 |
| `stylize`/look a cached glTF once, then clone: clones share materials. | `apps/katana-defense/src/main.ts`, lines 120-127 |
| Cap catch-up ticks (`maxTicksPerFrame: 2`) so heavy physics slows the game instead of spiralling. | `apps/rockfall/src/main.ts`, lines 324-331 |
| `"sim": { "build": "fast" }`: the SIMD Rapier build (Rockfall's fast capture holds 1,800 rocks); deterministic only for the same binary on the same machine. | `apps/breakpoint/scenes/site.json`, `apps/rockfall/src/main.ts` (`?build=fast`) |
| Physics in a Web Worker, packed state posted back each tick (transferred buffers, pooled). | `apps/breakpoint/src/game/sim.worker.ts`, lines 24-34 and 55-71 |
| Sample `world.bodyCounts()` every 30 frames only: it allocates. | `packages/sdk/src/game.ts` (`BODY_COUNT_INTERVAL`) |

| Gotcha | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| No allocation per frame | Preallocate vectors, typed arrays and event records; reuse the `{ ticks, alpha }` object `FixedStepLoop.advance` returns. |
| Instance keys must match | A new key is a new `InstancedMesh` (a new draw call). Vary colour per instance (the 5th argument), not material. |
| Workers need an inline path for captures | A worker runs on its own clock, so `?mode=fixed&ticks=n` (one tick per frame, `pnpm shot`) cannot be guaranteed through it. Put the sim behind one host interface with two implementations, a worker host and an inline host that runs the same sim code on the main thread, and pick inline whenever `mode` is `fixed` (and for a `?worker=0` debug switch). Node tests use the inline code too. |
| Worker wasm URL | Resolve the `?url` import against the page before posting it: `new URL(wasmUrl, location.href).href`. A worker resolves relative URLs against its own script, so a relative build base would otherwise point it at the wrong folder. See [sub-path-hosting.md](sub-path-hosting.md). |
| Budgets | Splats 1,500,000 (warns above); shadow cascades 3, max distance 120 m; DPR capped at 2. |
| Measure on an idle GPU | Benches: `node apps/<app>/bench/fps.mjs`; see [verification.md](../verification.md#benches-and-capture-scripts). |

See it in: [apps/rockfall/src/game/view/rock-view.ts](../../apps/rockfall/src/game/view/rock-view.ts) (spawned rocks into the registry, lines 68-101), [apps/swarm-siege/src/main.ts](../../apps/swarm-siege/src/main.ts) (worker only in realtime, inline otherwise, line 81; absolute wasm URL, lines 109-112; host choice, lines 133-135), [apps/swarm-siege/src/game/host.ts](../../apps/swarm-siege/src/game/host.ts) (`InlineHost` and `WorkerHost` behind one interface, lines 90 and 169-230), [apps/breakpoint/src/main.ts](../../apps/breakpoint/src/main.ts) (the same split, lines 85 and 125-157).


===== docs/cookbook/audio-sfx.md =====

# Audio and sound effects

Goal: sound cues driven by sim events, with no autoplay warnings and silent captures.

Every showcase game synthesises its sound with WebAudio (no audio files): one `AudioContext`, created on the first pointer or key press, a master gain, and one method per cue, fed from the sim's event queue after each tick.

```ts
export class Sfx {
	private ctx: AudioContext | null = null;
	private master: GainNode | null = null;
	constructor(readonly enabled: boolean) {
		if (!enabled) return;
		const unlock = (): void => {
			this.ctx ??= new AudioContext(); // only after a user gesture
			this.master = this.ctx.createGain();
			this.master.gain.value = 0.7;
			this.master.connect(this.ctx.destination);
			window.removeEventListener("pointerdown", unlock);
			window.removeEventListener("keydown", unlock);
		};
		window.addEventListener("pointerdown", unlock);
		window.addEventListener("keydown", unlock);
	}
	/** A short pitched blip; `gain` 0..1. */
	blip(freq: number, gain: number): void {
		const ctx = this.ctx, out = this.master;
		if (!ctx || !out) return; // not unlocked yet, or disabled
		const osc = ctx.createOscillator(), g = ctx.createGain(), t = ctx.currentTime;
		osc.frequency.value = freq;
		g.gain.setValueAtTime(gain, t);
		g.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.001, t + 0.15);
		osc.connect(g).connect(out);
		osc.start(t);
		osc.stop(t + 0.16);
	}
}

const sfx = new Sfx(q.get("mute") !== "1" && mode !== "fixed");
// after sim.step(input): for each event of this tick, e.g. if (ev === EV.HIT) sfx.blip(220, 0.4);
```

| Gotcha | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Never create the context at load | Chromium warns "The AudioContext was not allowed to start", and `pnpm shot` fails on any console warning. |
| Off in fixed mode | Captures and benches run with sound disabled (`mute || mode === "fixed"` in every game). |
| Sound is presentation | Play cues from the event queue after the tick; never let audio state feed back into the sim. |
| Rate-limit bursts | Cap voices per frame (Rockfall starts at most 4 impact sounds per rendered frame) or a rockslide clips. |
| Noise without `Math.random` | Fill noise buffers from a small LCG, as the games do, so nothing random appears near sim code. |
| Positional samples | `attachSound(object, listener, url)` from `@pebble3d/renderer` loads a file (cached) into a three.js `PositionalAudio` on an object; no showcase game uses it. |

See it in: [apps/rockfall/src/game/audio/sfx.ts](../../apps/rockfall/src/game/audio/sfx.ts) (gesture unlock, noise buffer, impact limit), [apps/chain-reaction/src/audio/sfx.ts](../../apps/chain-reaction/src/audio/sfx.ts), [apps/rockfall/src/main.ts](../../apps/rockfall/src/main.ts) (`sfx.handle(ev, sim)` per tick, line 377).


===== docs/cookbook/json-levels-and-headless-verify.md =====

# JSON levels and headless verify

Goal: levels as data files, each proven solvable by running the real engine sim in Node, with the result pinned by a state hash the browser must reproduce.

Chain Reaction's level format (`apps/chain-reaction/level.schema.json`) wraps a partial scene in puzzle metadata. `levels/01-first-drop.json` (a level file, not a scene, so no `"version"`; `hint` omitted):

```json
{
	"$schema": "../level.schema.json",
	"id": "01-first-drop",
	"name": "First Drop",
	"grid": { "cols": 12, "rows": 7, "origin": [-6, 0] },
	"ball": { "cell": [1, 6] },
	"goal": { "cell": [8, 0] },
	"inventory": { "ramp": 4 },
	"par": 1,
	"solution": [{ "part": "ramp", "cell": [1, 3], "dir": "right" }],
	"scene": {
		"entities": [
			{ "id": "slab", "prefab": "block", "transform": { "position": [-2, 0.5, 0], "scale": [8, 1, 1] } },
			{ "id": "backstop", "prefab": "block", "transform": { "position": [4.5, 1.5, 0], "scale": [3, 3, 1] } }
		]
	},
	"expect": { "tick": 213, "hash": "526cbffcde43ae4c" }
}
```

`composeLevel` deep-merges `scene` over `levels/base.json` (entities appended), adds the placed parts as prefab entities, then runs `parseScene` and `expandScene` like any scene. `PuzzleSim` spawns the result into a fresh `World` and steps it at 60 Hz. The browser and the CLI share that code.

```bash
pnpm --filter chain-reaction verify                 # all levels: "all 6 verified", exit 0
pnpm --filter chain-reaction verify 3               # one level (number, id or id prefix)
pnpm --filter chain-reaction verify --file /abs/my.json  # a level outside the campaign
pnpm --filter chain-reaction verify 3 --placements '[{"part":"fan","cell":[2,6],"dir":"right"}]'  # try a candidate
pnpm --filter chain-reaction verify --update        # rewrite each level's expect {tick, hash}
pnpm --filter chain-reaction verify --json          # machine-readable rows
node apps/chain-reaction/bench/agree.mjs            # browser hashes equal Node's (6/6)
```

The same approach for any game: a Node entry that loads the det wasm bytes (`loadSim("deterministic", readFileSync(...))`), builds the sim from the data file, runs a reference input or solution, and compares `world.stateHash()`.

## Spawn a scene and read state in Node

What `createGame` does at boot, without a browser (runs in a vitest test or a `node --experimental-strip-types` script):

```ts
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { expandScene } from "@pebble3d/sdk/expand";
import { parseScene } from "@pebble3d/sdk/schema";
import { loadSim, StateViews } from "@pebble3d/sdk/sim";

const bytes = readFileSync(new URL("../../../packages/sdk/wasm/det/engine_core_det_bg.wasm", import.meta.url));
const scene = parseScene(JSON.parse(readFileSync(new URL("../scenes/court.json", import.meta.url), "utf8")));
const handle = await loadSim("deterministic", bytes, { seed: scene.sim.seed, gravity: scene.sim.gravity });

// x.sim is SimEntry[]: { sceneId, desc }, in spawn order "__ground", "__bounds.<side>", then entities.
// desc is the engine's EntityDescJson; spawnScene(entries) calls world.spawn(JSON.stringify(e.desc)) for each.
const x = expandScene(scene);
const ids = handle.spawnScene(x.sim.filter((e) => !x.pendingHulls.includes(e.sceneId))); // Map sceneId -> sim id
const views = new StateViews(handle); // views.curr / views.prev / views.scratch over handle.memory

const ball = ids.get("ball") as number;
const slot = handle.world.slotOf(ball); // -1 if the entity has no slot
for (let t = 0; t < 120; t++) {
	handle.world.step(1);
	views.refresh(); // cheap no-op unless buffers moved; always call it after spawning or stepping
}
```
