2. Put each capture next to the look paragraph and the reference you chose. Write down, per capture, the three biggest gaps: "ground is flat grey", "the player disappears against the wall", "bloom washes out the HUD", "the sky does not match the sun".
3. Fix the biggest gaps, recapture the same ticks with the same seed, and compare side by side.
4. Repeat at least once more. Stop when a stranger would describe the capture in the brief's words.

Check the WebGL backend too (`--backend webgl`): fog, bloom and the toon pass must look the same there.

## Exit check

- The look paragraph in `BRIEF.md` names a palette with hex values, the style, the lighting and a reference capture.
- Captures of title, mid-play, the big moment and results match it; no engine-default grey ground or default sky remains unless the brief chose it.
- The player, the threat and the goal read in a thumbnail.
- At least two judge-and-improve passes, each with captures you opened.

Next: [complete-game-loop](../complete-game-loop/SKILL.md).


===== skills/complete-game-loop/SKILL.md =====

---
name: complete-game-loop
description: Use when a Pebble3D game plays but has no beginning or end, at the complete-loop step of make-a-game, or before calling a game finished. Adds title, play, results and restart, pause, the HUD, a demo bot that plays the whole loop, a README with controls and sourced numbers, and captures of every screen.
---

# Complete game loop

A mechanic you can play forever with no start screen, no goal and no ending is a prototype. A game has a title that says what to do, a round that can be won or lost, a results screen that says how you did, and a key that starts again. This skill wraps the core play in that loop and documents it.

Template: Ringout (`apps/ringout`) has every piece here at small scale: title with seat setup, countdown, rounds, an instant replay, results, rematch, a bot and a capture script. Read [its README](../../apps/ringout/README.md) and [app.ts](../../apps/ringout/src/game/app.ts) first.

## The phases

```
title → play → (win | lose) → results → restart → play ...
```

- **Phases are sim state.** Keep the phase in the sim and change it with a pure transition function, like Ronin Outpost's `nextPhase` in [phase.ts](../../apps/katana-defense/src/game/phase.ts): title, pre-wave, wave, wave clear, upgrade, victory, game over. A test can then drive the whole loop in Node, and the phase feeds the determinism hash.
- **Every play phase has an end.** A win condition and a lose condition from the brief, and if the game could stall, a limit (Ringout ends a round as a draw after a fight-tick limit, `MAX_FIGHT_TICKS` in [constants.ts](../../apps/ringout/src/game/constants.ts)).
- **Restart resets everything.** Score, timers, entities, the camera, the HUD and the seeded RNG (from a new or the same seed, as the brief says). A restart that leaks state from the last round is the most common loop bug: test it by playing two rounds in a row in Node and comparing the second round's hash with a fresh first round on the same seed.

## Title screen

- The game's name, one line on the goal, the controls in brief, and "press Enter" (or click). The brief's look applies here too: this is the first frame anyone sees.
- Put something alive behind it: a slow camera orbit over the arena (Ronin Outpost and Ringout both do), or an attract round played by the bot. Leave room on one side for the text.
- Any setup (players, difficulty, match length) lives here with keyboard shortcuts, as on Ringout's title.
- A `?title=1` style param that stays on the title helps the capture script.

## Play and the HUD

- The HUD shows only what the player needs to decide: the score or progress toward the goal, health or lives, a timer if time matters, and the state of the core verb (a cooldown, a meter, ammo). Ringout's HUD is a DOM overlay ([ui/hud.ts](../../apps/ringout/src/game/ui/hud.ts)); its look follows [art-direction](../art-direction/SKILL.md).
- Announce phase changes on screen: the round banner, "Wave clear", a countdown to the next hazard. A toast for big events (a knock-out, a new best).
- Show the controls somewhere on first play: a hint bar along the bottom, or the title.
- A `hud=0` param hides it for clean captures.

## Pause

- Esc (or P) pauses: stop stepping the sim, freeze presentation time, mute or duck sound, and show a small panel with resume, restart and quit to title. In a one-screen local game, Esc may simply return to the title, as Ringout does.
- Pause when the tab is hidden too, so time does not pile up: Breakpoint listens for `visibilitychange` ([main.ts](../../apps/breakpoint/src/main.ts)). Clear held keys on window blur, or the player keeps running after alt-tab.
- Pause is not sim input in a replayable game: it stops ticks, it is not recorded as a tick.

## Results and restart

- Say who won or what the outcome was, in big type, then the numbers that matter for this game: score, time, best, per-player stats (Ringout shows wins, knock-outs, dashes and the hardest hit per seat). Show a personal best if the brief wants replay value.
- One key restarts, one returns to the title. Name both on the screen.
- **Lock confirm keys briefly** when a results or replay screen appears, so a player still mashing the action key does not skip it. Ringout's `MenuGate` swallows Enter and Space for `LOCK = 0.75` s ([gate.ts](../../apps/ringout/src/game/gate.ts)).
- Optional but strong: an instant replay of the decisive moment before results, re-simulated from the input log, as Ringout and Breakpoint do.

## The demo bot plays the whole loop

`?demo=1` drives everything through the same input type a player produces: it presses start on the title, plays the round to a win or a loss, waits on results, and restarts. Expose `phase` and the bot's current action as `__pebble3d.game` probes so captures and sidecars show where it is. The pattern: [demo-bot-and-captures.md](../../docs/cookbook/demo-bot-and-captures.md). Pin the ticks of the loop's key moments (first win, results, restart) in a test so a rule change that moves them fails loudly.

**The bot must finish the loop on most seeds, not just one.** A bot that loses or stalls on most seeds makes every capture of results, replay and restart luck. Write a Node test that runs the bot headless over a range of seeds, counts the runs that reach the results phase within a tick limit, and asserts that share is a clear majority. A sketch, with your own sim and bot names:

```ts
it("the demo bot reaches results on most seeds", () => {
	let reached = 0;
	const seeds = Array.from({ length: 20 }, (_, i) => i + 1);
	for (const seed of seeds) {
		const sim = makeSim(seed);
		const bot = makeBot(sim);
		while (sim.phase !== "results" && sim.tick < MAX_TICKS) sim.step(bot.next());
		if (sim.phase === "results") reached++;
		sim.free();
	}
	expect(reached / seeds.length).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0.8);
});
```

If it fails, tune the bot (its aim, timing, which threat it picks), not the game: the rules and numbers in the brief are the player's game, and weakening them so the bot wins changes what you ship. Where the brief wants the bot to show a loss too, assert that separately on a fixed seed.

## README

`apps/<name>/README.md`, with the sections of [Ringout's README](../../apps/ringout/README.md):

1. **What it is**: the pitch in a paragraph, with the game's key numbers.
2. **Run it**: the install, dev and test commands with the URL, then a table of every URL param the game reads (`demo`, `seed`, `mode`, `ticks`, `backend`, `hud`, `mute`, and the game's own).
3. **Controls**: a table of every input, per screen. Check each line against the input code; a control the README invents is a bug.
4. **What it shows off**: the engine features it exercises, each in a sentence.
5. **Known issues**: what is rough, honestly.

**Every number is sourced.** Each number in the README comes from a constant in the code, a test, or a measurement you ran (say how: backend, machine, idle GPU). Ringout's "61 hexagonal basalt columns in 5 rings" is `RINGS = 5` in [constants.ts](../../apps/ringout/src/game/constants.ts). Do not round up, guess fps, or keep a number after the constant changes.

## Captures

`apps/<name>/bench/capture-final.sh`, after [Ringout's](../../apps/ringout/bench/capture-final.sh): build once, then one shot per moment with `--param demo=1` and a fixed seed, stopping on the first failure. Cover at least the title, mid-play, the big moment, a win or a loss, the results screen and one `--sequence` of the core action. Run it, read every sidecar and open every PNG the shot prints, as [verify-your-work](../verify-your-work/SKILL.md) says.

Putting the game on the project site is a separate step, only when the developer asks: [site/README.md](../../site/README.md) lists the entry, the WebP conversion and the claim checks.

## Exit check

- Title → play → win or lose → results → restart works by keyboard, and by the `?demo=1` bot with no human input.
- The bot test passes: over a range of seeds, a clear majority of `?demo=1` runs reach results.
- Pause, tab-hide and Esc behave; restart leaves no state from the last round (tested in Node).
- The HUD shows what the player needs, and hides with `hud=0`.
- The README lists how to run it, the controls and every URL param, and every number in it has a source.
- The capture script covers every screen, and you opened every capture.

Next: [verify-your-work](../verify-your-work/SKILL.md), the full check.


===== skills/genre-playbooks/SKILL.md =====

---
name: genre-playbooks
description: Use when a Pebble3D game request fits a known genre (racer, platformer, tower defence, physics puzzle, stealth, sandbox, arena brawler, horde action, demolition), at the build step of make-a-game, to reuse the shipped demo that already does that genre well.
---

# Genre playbooks

Each shipped demo in `apps/` is a worked answer to one genre. A playbook points you at that demo, names the systems the genre needs, the feel points that matter, and the checks that prove the genre works. It does not replace the demo: open it, read its README, and copy its structure before inventing your own.

Load this at the build step of [make-a-game](../make-a-game/SKILL.md), after [engine-pitfalls](../engine-pitfalls/SKILL.md). Polish comes later from [game-feel](../game-feel/SKILL.md) and the definition of done from [verify-your-work](../verify-your-work/SKILL.md); the playbooks only add what is specific to the genre.

## Pick the closest playbook

Read the brief (`apps/<name>/BRIEF.md`) and match the core verb, not the theme. A game about cats racing across rooftops is a platformer or a racer depending on whether the player steers a path or beats a clock.

| The player mainly...                                        | Playbook                            | Demo to study                               |
| ----------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| Steers a vehicle against a clock or a ghost                 | [racer](racer.md)                   | [drift-drone](../../apps/drift-drone)       |
| Runs and jumps across platforms                             | [platformer](platformer.md)         | [skyrun](../../apps/skyrun)                 |
| Places defences and watches waves hit them                  | [tower defence](tower-defence.md)   | [swarm-siege](../../apps/swarm-siege)       |
| Sets up parts, then runs a machine                          | [physics puzzle](physics-puzzle.md) | [chain-reaction](../../apps/chain-reaction) |
| Sneaks past watchers to a goal                              | [stealth](stealth.md)               | [lanternfall](../../apps/lanternfall)       |
| Builds and edits freely with physics                        | [sandbox](sandbox.md)               | [pebble-garden](../../apps/pebble-garden)   |
| Shoves rivals in a shared arena (local multiplayer or bots) | [arena brawler](arena-brawler.md)   | [ringout](../../apps/ringout)               |
| Fights a crowd of melee enemies in waves                    | [horde action](horde-action.md)     | [katana-defense](../../apps/katana-defense) |
| Breaks structures with projectiles                          | [demolition](demolition.md)         | [breakpoint](../../apps/breakpoint)         |

Games often blend two genres. Pick the one that owns the core verb as the base and borrow single systems from the second (for example, a racer with a tower-defence-style upgrade screen).

## When none fits

There is no playbook for fighters, online multiplayer or any genre without a shipped demo. Do not invent one. Use the nearest playbook for structure and the cookbook in [docs/cookbook/](../../docs/cookbook/README.md) for single techniques, and say so: add a line to the assumptions in `BRIEF.md` such as "No playbook for this genre; built on the arena-brawler structure". Tell the developer in your first progress message too.

## How to use a playbook

1. Read the demo README end to end, then the cited source files.
2. Copy the sim/presentation split. The sim is deterministic and seeded; the view only reads it. Every playbook assumes this.
3. Build the genre's core systems first and cover them with sim tests before any art.
4. Before the feel pass, run the genre-specific checks in the playbook. They are in addition to the checks in [verify-your-work](../verify-your-work/SKILL.md), not instead of them.

## Rockfall (`apps/rockfall`): custom boot, engine spawners, 1,800 bodies

## Breakpoint (`apps/breakpoint`): demolition, physics in a worker

| `fast` build | `apps/breakpoint/scenes/site.json` (42-45) | SIMD Rapier. |

## Field Notes (`apps/field-notes`): splat sites, depth of field

| Live splat grade | `apps/katana-defense/src/game/view/dusk.ts` (136-145) | `renderer.splatColor` exposure, saturation, tint over the dusk cycle. |

## Skyrun (`apps/skyrun`): parkour time trial, riding kinematic movers

| Movers driven before each step | `apps/skyrun/src/game/sim.ts` (201-216) | `setKinematicPose` for the pose reached in this tick's `world.step`. |
| Jump buffer on top of the engine's coyote time | `apps/skyrun/src/game/sim.ts` (218-236) | A press 8 ticks before landing still jumps. |
| Respawn with `teleport` | `apps/skyrun/src/game/sim.ts` (271-279) | Clears the character's vertical and platform velocity. |
| Ghost re-simulated from the input log | `apps/skyrun/src/game/ghost.ts` (92-124) | Second sim in lockstep; a run that does not finish on its recorded tick is hidden. `courseFingerprint` (`course.ts`, 339) discards records from another layout. |
| `CharacterView` on an app-managed avatar | `apps/skyrun/src/game/view/runner-view.ts` (125-126) | Cross-faded clips and facing without `createGame`. |
| Spring-arm camera on a custom world | `apps/skyrun/src/game/view/camera-rig.ts` (35-48) | `ThirdPersonController` with a static-only ray into the sim's own world. |
| Painted sky and matched fog | `apps/skyrun/src/game/view/sky.ts` (55-68) | Replaces `backgroundNode` and `fogNode` after `createRenderer`. |
| Sub-path hosting | `apps/skyrun/src/main.ts` (86-93) | Root-absolute `/assets/...` and `/basis/` resolved by the renderer's asset base (`VITE_PEBBLE3D_ASSET_BASE`, else Vite's `BASE_URL`). |

## Lanternfall (`apps/lanternfall`): a generated keep, raycast guards

## Ringout (`apps/ringout`): sumo with impulses, kinematic movers, replay

| Feature | File (lines) | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |

| Torque and impulse drive | `apps/ringout/src/game/sim.ts` (207-213) | `applyImpulse` to steer plus `applyTorqueImpulse` about the rolling axis, capped by speed along the stick. |
| Dash | `apps/ringout/src/game/sim.ts` (214-230) | One large impulse with a cooldown, grounded and not staggered. |
| Arena turned by kinematic poses | `apps/ringout/src/game/sim.ts` (294-306) | Every column's pose from the arena angle, the shake and the fall, via `setKinematicPose`. |
| Velocity reads | `apps/ringout/src/game/sim.ts` (322-331) | `linearVelocity` and `angularVelocity` into the scratch buffer every tick. |
| Round hash | `apps/ringout/src/game/sim.ts` (458-478) | Engine `stateHash` plus every rule variable. |
| Instant replay and its proof | `apps/ringout/src/game/app.ts` (240-256, 267-283) | Fresh `RoundSim` from the seed, fed the input log; the final hash is compared on screen. |
| Independent worlds from one module | `apps/ringout/src/game/physics.ts` (15-23) | New `World`s from the already-loaded deterministic wasm. |

===== README.md =====

# Pebble3D

A browser 3D engine: three.js 0.187 (WebGPU, with a WebGL fallback) for rendering, a Rust/WASM Rapier crate for physics, and Gaussian-splat environments. Scenes are plain JSON, validated by a schema, so an agent can write one without reading engine code.

## Agent skills

Ask a coding agent for a game in plain words and it does not start by writing code. The [agent skills](skills/README.md) in `skills/` have it ask at most six short questions (or write down defaults when it cannot ask), write a `BRIEF.md` for you to approve, then build a complete game: title, play, results and restart, with game feel, one committed art direction and a `?demo=1` bot. It verifies the game with tests and screenshots it has looked at before it reports done.

Start with [skills/make-a-game/SKILL.md](skills/make-a-game/SKILL.md), which runs the others in this order: interview, brief, scaffold, build, game feel, art pass, complete loop, verify. Claude Code, Cursor and GitHub Copilot discover the copies in `.claude/skills/`; other agents find them through [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) and [llms.txt](llms.txt). Overview: https://pebble3d.github.io/pebble3d/build-with-ai/skills/.

## Quickstart

Requires Node 22.6 or newer (the Node scripts use `--experimental-strip-types`; the avatar GLB hash was verified on Node 25.2.1, see `.nvmrc`), pnpm, a Rust toolchain with the `wasm32-unknown-unknown` target, and `wasm-bindgen-cli` 0.2.130. `pnpm shot` also needs a Chromium for Playwright: run `pnpm exec playwright install chromium` once.

```bash
pnpm i && pnpm build:wasm && pnpm fetch-assets && pnpm dev
```

`pnpm dev` serves the playground with Vite (default port 5173). Open `/?scene=showcase` (a splat scene with a realistic human character). Other scenes: `showcase-robot` (the same scene with the stylised robot), `studio`, `outdoor`, `det`, `showcase-badsplat`.

Playground URL params: `scene`, `mode=realtime|fixed`, `ticks`, `backend=webgpu|webgl`, `cam`, `overlay`, `script`, `splat`, `debug=splatOnly`. The stats overlay toggles with the backtick key.

## Docs for humans and LLMs

Start with [docs/getting-started.md](docs/getting-started.md), then browse [docs/](docs/) (scene and API reference, cookbook, verification, troubleshooting). Coding agents: read [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md). LLMs can discover everything from [llms.txt](llms.txt), or load [llms-full.txt](llms-full.txt) in one go.

## Showcase games

Original games, each built to show off one strength of the engine. Each one plays a full loop, includes an autoplayer bot (`?demo=1`), and has unit tests. Run `pnpm --filter <app> dev`, then open the port listed below. Each game's README (`apps/<app>/README.md`) covers its controls, URL params, numbers and known issues. Play them online at https://pebble3d.github.io/pebble3d/demos/.

| Game           | App              | Port | What it shows off                                                                                                                                            |
| -------------- | ---------------- | ---- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Ronin Outpost  | `katana-defense` | 5180 | Toon-shaded ninja katana horde defence: Rocketbox avatars, procedural combat animation with IK, skinned zombie crowds, and the opt-in `post.style: "toon"`   |
| Breakpoint     | `breakpoint`     | 5210 | Physics demolition with 838 to 1,344 Rapier bodies per site, run in a Web Worker on the `fast` build, plus a deterministic replay of your best shot          |
| Ghostline      | `ghostline`      | 5220 | Marble time trials with ghosts recomputed live from your inputs (not recordings), PBR materials and JSON courses                                             |
| Field Notes    | `field-notes`    | 5231 | Photography in two real Gaussian-splat captures: splat/mesh compositing, a third-person controller, and depth of field                                       |
| Rockfall       | `rockfall`       | 5240 | Survival against waves driven by Rust-side seeded spawners, with up to 1,800 live bodies                                                                     |
| Chain Reaction | `chain-reaction` | 5250 | A contraption puzzle whose levels are JSON scenes; `pnpm --filter chain-reaction verify` replays each solution headless in Node and matches the browser hash |
| Lanternfall    | `lanternfall`    | 5260 | A stealth heist in a keep generated from a seed as schema-valid scene JSON, with raycast guard perception and `accel` characters                             |
| Ringout        | `ringout`        | 5270 | Local multiplayer sumo: torque and impulse-driven orbs on a collapsing arena of kinematic columns, with an instant replay checked against the live hash      |
| Skyrun         | `skyrun`         | 5280 | A parkour time trial: the character controller riding sliding, spinning and orbiting platforms (`ridePlatforms`), with a re-simulated ghost                  |
| Pebble Garden  | `pebble-garden`  | 5290 | A physics sandbox and level editor: gardens export as schema-valid scene JSON, import with readable errors, and play and rewind exactly                      |
| Swarm Siege    | `swarm-siege`    | 5300 | Tower defence against thousands of instanced enemies simulated in a Web Worker, with raycast camera picking and spawner debris                               |
| Drift Drone    | `drift-drone`    | 5310 | An FPV drone flown by thrust and torque impulses through a Gaussian-splat capture, with a re-simulated ghost and a depth-of-field photo finish               |
| Flowroll       | `flowroll`       | 5390 | Brazilian jiu-jitsu as positional chess: a deterministic position graph of moves and counters, hand-keyed jointed mannequins, and a replay of the finish     |

Linux Chromium needs WebGPU switched on: `chromium --enable-unsafe-webgpu --enable-features=Vulkan --use-angle=vulkan`. If WebGPU isn't available, `?backend=webgl` uses the WebGL fallback.

## A minimal scene

```json
{
	"version": 1,
	"environment": { "preset": "studio", "ground": {} },
	"prefabs": {
		"ball": {
			"mesh": { "primitive": "sphere" },
			"body": { "restitution": 0.5 }
		}
	},
	"entities": [
		{ "id": "b1", "prefab": "ball", "transform": { "position": [0, 4, 0] } }
	]
}
```

Save it as `apps/playground/scenes/mine.json` and open `/?scene=mine`.

## For agents

[`packages/sdk/scene.schema.json`](packages/sdk/scene.schema.json) is the JSON Schema for scene files (regenerate with `pnpm --filter @pebble3d/sdk schema`). Point `$schema` at it and validate before running. The zod source is `packages/sdk/src/schema.ts`. In a page, `window.__pebble3d` exposes `ready`, `done`, `stats()`, `stateHash()`, `setCamera()`, `player()` and `position()`.

## Screenshots: `pnpm shot`

```bash
pnpm shot --scene showcase --cam hero --backend webgpu --overlay
```

It builds the app (default the playground), serves it on a free port, renders in fixed-tick mode in Chromium and writes `artifacts/shots/<scene>-<cam>-<backend>-<w>x<h>.png` plus a `.json` sidecar (`adapterInfo`, `stats`, `stateHash`, `tick`, console).

| Flag                                          | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `--scene <name>`                              | A file in `apps/playground/scenes/`. Required for the playground (the default app); optional with `--app`.                                                                                                                                                               |
| `--cam <preset>`                              | A camera preset, or `controller`. Default: the renderer's (`hero`, else the first preset).                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `--backend webgpu\|webgl`                     | Default `webgpu`. Fails if that backend is not the one that ran.                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `--size WxH` / `--resize WxH`                 | Viewport size (default 1280x720) / resize after load (not with `--sequence`).                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `--ticks <n>`                                 | Sim ticks to run before capture (default 120).                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `--script <name>`                             | Scripted player input: `walk-forward`, `walk-into-crates`, `walk-to-bounds`, `walk-side`, `sprint-side`, `jump`, `jump-side` (see `SCRIPTS` in `apps/playground/src/main.ts`).                                                                                           |
| `--sequence <n>[:<every>]`                    | Capture `n` frames, one every `<every>` ticks (default 1), from tick `--ticks`: `<name>-f000.png`... plus `<name>.webp`, an animated WebP (30 fps for every=1, else real time). `--fps <n>` / `--scale <f>` / `--no-frames` override the rate, downscale, drop the PNGs. |
| `--overlay`                                   | Show the stats overlay in the shot.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `--splat <url>` / `--debug splatOnly`         | Override the splat / draw only the splat.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `--allow-console-error "<substring>[:count]"` | Permit an expected console error, optionally with an exact count.                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `--no-build` / `--headed`                     | Skip the build / show the browser.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `--app <dir>` / `--param key=value`           | Capture another app under `apps/` (then `--scene` is optional) / pass extra URL params.                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `--out <dir>` / `--name <basename>`           | Output directory (inside `artifacts/`) / file basename.                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `--timeout <s>` / `--port <n>`                | Per-wait timeout (default 60) / serve the preview on a fixed port.                                                                                                                                                                                                       |

It exits 1 on any console warning or error not in `scripts/shot/console-allowlist.json` or an `--allow-console-error`, on a missing or software (SwiftShader) adapter, or if a wait (load, `__pebble3d.done`, each sequence frame) exceeds `--timeout` (default 60 s).

## Tests and benchmarks

```bash
cargo test -p engine-core --features deterministic
cargo test -p engine-core --no-default-features --features fast
pnpm -r test && pnpm -r typecheck && pnpm lint
node --experimental-strip-types packages/sdk/test/determinism.mjs --expect "$(cat packages/sdk/test/fixtures/det-hash.txt)"
pnpm shot --scene det --cam hero --backend webgpu --ticks 1000
node -e "const s=require('./artifacts/shots/det-hero-webgpu-1280x720.json'); const h=require('fs').readFileSync('packages/sdk/test/fixtures/det-hash.txt','utf8').trim(); process.exit(s.stateHash===h && s.tick===1000 ? 0 : 1)"
node --experimental-strip-types packages/sdk/test/bench.mjs
```

`engine-core` defaults to the `deterministic` feature (Rapier enhanced-determinism, bit-identical state hash across runs); `fast` is plain Rapier with WASM SIMD. The Node scripts need `--experimental-strip-types` because they import TypeScript sources.

Bench (10,000 ticks at 1/60 s, 300 active ticks sampled, real-time multiple of the sim step, one run on an AMD RDNA 3 laptop; numbers vary run to run):

| Build         | Bodies | Active ticks (x real time) | Full 10k run (x real time) |
| ------------- | ------ | -------------------------- | -------------------------- |
| deterministic | 100    | 231                        | 2890                       |
| deterministic | 500    | 109                        | 1623                       |
| fast          | 100    | 368                        | 2817                       |
| fast          | 500    | 149                        | 1608                       |

"Full run" includes the stretch where bodies are asleep.

## Known limitations

- One game per page: `Game.dispose` does not exist yet (planned).
- Determinism is verified on V8 (Node and Chromium) only.
- The derived splat hash was verified on one machine. If `fetch-assets` reports a hash mismatch elsewhere, that is the cause.
- The splat is a drone capture, so grass is soft and blurry up close.
- On `showcase-robot`, the walk clip's toe dips about 6 cm below the ground plane.
- On `showcase-robot`, there is no fall animation clip; falling reuses the jump clip.
- On the human, residual foot slip is about 15% at walk and 24% at sprint, inherited from the source clips.
- The human avatar (`rocketbox-male-adult-16.glb`) builds only on linux-x64, because the pinned KTX-Software binary is linux-x64 only. On other platforms `pnpm fetch-assets` reports that asset as failed; use `?scene=showcase-robot`.
- The overlay's draw calls and triangles count every pass (AO prepass, shadow cascades, bloom, SMAA), not just the main scene.
- Screenshots repeat to RMSE < 0.002 (under 0.1% of pixels more than 8/255 off), not byte for byte.
- `fps` and `frameMs` are wall-clock. In fixed mode the sim time is not the wall time.

## Assets and credits

Large assets are not committed; `pnpm fetch-assets` downloads them per `apps/playground/assets.manifest.json`. Licenses and attribution (Poly Haven HDRI, CC BY 4.0 splat scene, Quaternius robot, and the showcase character: Microsoft Rocketbox `Male_Adult_16`, MIT, Copyright (c) 2020 Microsoft) are in [`apps/playground/public/assets/LICENSES.md`](apps/playground/public/assets/LICENSES.md). The full Rocketbox licence text is in [`Microsoft-Rocketbox-MIT.txt`](apps/playground/public/assets/licenses/Microsoft-Rocketbox-MIT.txt). The Basis transcoder served at `/basis/` is Apache-2.0; its notice ships in `dist/basis/`.

## Roadmap

- `packages/mcp-server`: an MCP server for authoring, running and screenshotting scenes.
- A headless CLI runner.
- Spatial-query and diagnostics APIs for agents.
- A full studio HUD beyond the stats overlay (`packages/studio-overlay`).
- `scripts/splat-collider`: generate physics geometry from a splat capture.
- Tighter fast-build performance at 500 bodies.

   free license in Section 2 does not apply to You. To use the Software,
   You must first obtain a separate commercial license from the Licensor,
   on terms agreed in writing with the Licensor.

   If Your Annual Revenue first reaches the Threshold while You are using
   the Software under Section 2, You have sixty (60) days from that date to
   obtain a commercial license or to stop using the Software. Products You
   distributed before that date may remain in the hands of their end users.

4. Conditions

   (a) You must keep this license file and all copyright notices with every
       copy or substantial portion of the Software You distribute.
   (b) Anyone who receives the Software from You receives it under this
       license, and the Annual Revenue conditions apply to them separately.
   (c) You may not remove or bypass the Annual Revenue conditions by
       sublicensing the Software under different terms, or by splitting
       Your business across entities.
   (d) The Licensor may ask You in writing to confirm that Your Annual
       Revenue is under the Threshold. You must answer truthfully within
       thirty (30) days.

5. End Users

   End users of a game or application You build with the Software do not
   need their own license to play or use it.

6. Termination

   If You breach this license and do not fix the breach within thirty (30)
   days of written notice from the Licensor, Your rights under this license
   end automatically. Sections 7, 8 and 9 survive termination.
